semin-durr:16-16.t:
His saying: {فَلاَ يَصُدَّنَّكَ عَنْهَا مَن لاَّ يُؤْمِنُ بِهَا}: {مَن لاَّ يُؤْمِنُ} is the one prohibited in outward form, but someone else is meant; so it belongs to the type «لا أُرَيَنَّك هَهنا» ("let me not see you here"). It has also been said: the unbeliever's turning [him] away from believing in it is a cause of denial, so the cause is mentioned to indicate the effect. The two pronouns in «عنها» and «بها» refer to the Hour. It has also been said: to the prayer. And it has been said: in «عنها» to the prayer, and in «بها» to the Hour.

His saying: {فتردى}: it may be accusative (manṣūb) in answer to the prohibition, by an implied «أنْ»; or it may be nominative (marfūʿ) as the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "فأنت تردى" (so you would perish). Yaḥyā read «تردى» with a kasra on the tāʾ, and it has already been stated that this is a dialect. al-radā is destruction; one says: رَدِيَ يردى رَدى.
Durayd ibn al-Ṣimma said:
3283 - تنادَوْا فقالوا أَرْدَتِ الخيلُ فارساً ... فقلتُ أَعَبْدُ اللهِ ذلكُمُ الرَّدِي
(They called out to one another, saying: "The horses have brought down a horseman"; I said: "Is it ʿAbd Allāh, that one who has perished?")

semin-durr:17-17.t:
His saying: {وَمَا تِلْكَ بِيَمِينِكَ}: «ما» is an interrogative mubtadaʾ (subject), and «تلك» is its khabar (predicate). «بيمنيك» [Translator's note: so spelled in the source, for «بيمينك».] is attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted, because it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), like His saying: {وهذا بَعْلِي شَيْخاً} [Hūd: 72]. The governor of the implied ḥāl is the meaning of pointing. al-Zamakhsharī allowed «تلك» to be a relative noun meaning «التي», with «بيمينك» as its ṣila (relative clause), and Ibn ʿAṭiyya mentioned nothing else. This is not the doctrine of the Basrans, because they do not make any demonstrative a relative noun except «ذا», under conditions I mentioned at the beginning of this book. As for the Kufans, they allow it in all of them, and this verse is an instance of it according to them, i.e. "and what is that which is in your right hand", and they also cited:
3284 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ...
نَجَوْتِ وهذا تحملينَ طَليقُ
(You have escaped, and the one you carry is free.)
i.e. "and the one whom you carry".

semin-durr:18-18.t:
His saying: {هِيَ عَصَايَ}: «هي» refers back to the thing asked about. The generality read «عصايَ» with a fatḥa on the yāʾ, while al-Jaḥdarī and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read «عَصَيَّ» with conversion and assimilation. The justification of that has already been given at the beginning of al-Baqara, together with to whom this dialect is attributed and the poetry transmitted about it. It is also reported from Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Abī Isḥāq: «عَصَاْيْ» with the yāʾ quiescent in continuous recitation. Nāfiʿ did the like in «مَحْيَاْيْ», combining two quiescent letters in continuous recitation, and the discussion of it has already been given there.

His saying: {أَتَوَكَّأُ}: it may be a second khabar (predicate) of «هي»; and it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial), either from «عصايَ» or from the yāʾ. There is remoteness in that, because a ḥāl coming from the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive) is rare, and besides it has conditions, none of which is present here. It may also be a resumptive clause. Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed, transmitting from someone else, that «عصايَ» be accusative by an implied verb, with «أتوكَّأُ» as the khabar; but that should not be said.
al-tawakkuʾ is leaning one's weight on something; it has the meaning of al-ittikāʾ. Its explanation has already been given in Yūsuf; the two are from a single root, and I have mentioned it here because their patterns differ.
al-hashsh, with the dotted [shīn], is beating [leaves down]. One says: هَشَشْتُ الوَرَقَ أَهُشُّه, i.e. I beat it so that it falls. As for هَشَّ يَهِش with a kasra on the middle radical in the imperfect, it has the meaning of cheerfulness (al-bashāsha). al-Nakhaʿī read it that way, and it was said: it has the meaning of أهُشُّ with ḍamma, and the object is omitted in both readings, i.e. "I beat down the leaves" or "the trees". It was also said: in this reading it is from هَشَّ هَشاشةً, when something inclines. al-Ḥasan and ʿIkrima read «وأَهُسُّ» with a ḍamma on the hāʾ and with the undotted sīn, which is driving [animals]; from it come al-hass and al-hasās. On this [reading] it ought to be transitive by itself, but it was made to imply (ḍummina) the meaning of a verb that is made transitive with «على», and that is sounder. Ibn Khālawayh transmitted from al-Nakhaʿī that he read «وأُهِشُّ» with a ḍamma on the hamza and a kasra on the hāʾ, from the four-letter «أَهَشَّ», with the undotted [sīn]; al-Zamakhsharī transmitted it from him with the dotted [shīn]; so there are several readings from him.
The author of «al-Lawāmiḥ» transmitted from Mujāhid and ʿIkrima «وأَهُشُ» with a ḍamma on the hāʾ and a light (undoubled) shīn, and said: "I know no justification for it", unless he found the doubling heavy together with the diffusion (tafashshī) of the shīn and so lightened it; and it has the meaning of the generality's reading.
Some read «غَنْمي» with a sukūn on the nūn, and that is not by analogy. al-maʾārib is the plural of maʾraba, which is need; likewise al-irba. In the rāʾ of «المأربة» all three vowels occur.
«أخرى» is like His saying: {الأسمآء الحسنى} [al-Isrāʾ: 110], which was treated shortly before. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Had it been said «أُخَر», it would have been according to the wording", meaning «أُخَر» with a ḍamma on the hamza and a fatḥa on the khāʾ, and by "the wording" the plural form. al-Ahwāzī transmitted from Shayba and al-Zuhrī «مارب», saying "without hamza", stating it unqualified like that. What is meant by "without hamza" is without a fully realised hamza, rather a hamza eased "between the two" (bayna bayna); otherwise dropping it altogether would be anomalous (shādhdh).

semin-durr:20-20.t: His saying: {تسعى}: it may be a second khabar (predicate), according to those who allow that. It may also be a naʿt (adjective) of «حيَّة».

semin-durr:21-21.t:
His saying: {سِيَرتَهَا}: there are several views on its accusative. First: that it is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), i.e. "in its sīra", i.e. its manner. Second: that it is accusative as a badal (substitute) of the «ها» of «سنعيدها», a substitute of inclusion (badal ishtimāl), because al-sīra is the state, i.e. "We shall restore it, its state and its shape". Third: that it is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "to its sīra". al-Zamakhsharī said: "It may be an object, from عاده meaning 'he returned to it', so it becomes transitive to two objects; from this is the verse of Zuhayr:
3285 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وعادَكَ أَنْ تُلاَقِيَها العَداءُ
(... and the obstacles returned to you [preventing you] from meeting her.)
This is the meaning of the statement of whoever said it is by dropping «إلى»." He had also allowed it to be an adverb, as stated above. However, al-Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] rejected that on the ground that it is a specific (mukhtaṣṣ) adverb, and the verb does not reach it except through the mediation of «في», except in what is anomalous.
al-sīra is of the pattern fiʿla, indicating the manner, from al-sayr (going), like al-rikba from al-rukūb (riding); then its usage was widened and it was used for the way and the method. Khālid al-Hudhalī said:
3286 - فلا تغْضَبَنْ مِنْ سِيرَةٍ أنت سِرْتَها ... فأولُ راضٍ سيرةً مَنْ يَسِيرُها
(Do not be angry at a way that you yourself followed; the first to be pleased with a way is the one who follows it.)
He also allowed it to be accusative by an implied verb, i.e. "it goes its going (yasīru sīratahā) the first", this implied clause being in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "We shall restore it going its way".

semin-durr:22-22.t:
His saying: {واضمم}: there must be an omission here; the implied form is: "Draw in your hand, and it will be drawn in; and bring it out, and it will come out". So something was omitted from the first and from the second, and their counterparts were kept to indicate that, for concision and brevity. This was needed only because the coming out does not result from the mere drawing in.

His saying: {بَيْضَآءَ}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «تَخْرُجْ».

His saying: {مِنْ غَيْرِ سواء}: it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «تخرجْ»; it may be attached to «بيضاءَ» because of the verbal meaning in it, as in: "it became white without blemish". And it may be attached to something omitted, as a ḥāl from the pronoun in «بيضاء». His saying {مِنْ غَيْرِ سواء} is called by the rhetoricians "al-iḥtirās" (precaution), which is to bring something that removes the misapprehension of one who might imagine other than what is meant; for whiteness may mean leprosy and vitiligo, so He brought His saying {مِنْ غَيْرِ سواء} to negate that.
[Translator's note: the Quranic text reads «سُوءٍ»; the source spells it «سواء» here.]

His saying: {آيَةً}: there are several views on it. First: that it is a ḥāl, I mean that it is a badal (substitute) of «بيضاءَ», which occurs as a ḥāl. Second: that it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «بيضاءَ». Third: that it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in the preposition and its genitive noun. Fourth: that it is accusative by an omitted verb. Abū al-Baqāʾ implied it as: "We made it a sign", or "We gave you a sign". al-Zamakhsharī implied it as: "take a sign", and he also implied: "here is (dūnaka) a sign". al-Shaykh rejected the latter on the ground that it belongs to the category of incitement (al-ighrāʾ), and it is not permitted to imply [verbal] adverbs in incitement. He said: because the governor has been omitted and this [adverb] stands in its place, so it is not permitted to omit the substitute as well. Moreover, their rules differ from those of the explicit governor, so they may not be implied, even if implying verbs is permitted.
[Translator's note: «دنوكَ» in the source is evidently «دونكَ», as the following discussion of ighrāʾ shows.]

semin-durr:23-23.t:
His saying: {لِنُرِيَكَ}: attached (mutaʿalliq) to what «آية» indicates, i.e. "We gave indication by it in order to show you", or to the implied "We made it" or "We gave you". al-Zamakhsharī implied it as: "In order to show you, We did that". al-Ḥūfī allowed it to be attached to «اضْمُمْ», and someone else allowed it to be attached to «تَخْرُجْ». It may not be attached to the word «آية» itself, because it has been qualified. al-Zamakhsharī also implied it as: "In order to show you, take this sign as well".

His saying: {مِنْ آيَاتِنَا الكبرى}: «مِنْ آياتنا» may be attached to something omitted, as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الكبرى», «الكبرى» being on this view the second object of «نُرِيَكَ». The implied form is: "In order to show you the greatest, it being from Our signs", i.e. some of Our signs. Alternatively, the second object may be «مِنْ آياتنا» itself, so it is also attached to something omitted, and «الكبرى» on this view is a naʿt (adjective) of «آياتنا», a feminine plural of non-rational beings described with the description of a singular, in the manner of {مَآرِبُ أخرى} [Ṭā Hā: 18] and {الأسمآء الحسنى} [al-Isrāʾ: 110].
These two views were transmitted by al-Zamakhsharī, al-Ḥūfī, Abū al-Baqāʾ and Ibn ʿAṭiyya. al-Shaykh chose the second, saying: "Because it follows from that that all His signs are the greatest ones; for whatever is one of the greatest [signs] can truly be called 'the greatest'. If you make «الكبرى» a second object, the signs are not described as greatest, since it is it [the object] that is described with the elative (afʿal al-tafḍīl). Also, if you make «الكبرى» an object, it cannot be a description of the staff and the hand together, since that would require the dual; nor is it permissible to single out one of them with the description to the exclusion of the other, because the preference is present in each of them. And what al-Ḥasan said is far-fetched: that the hand is greater in miraculousness than the staff; for he made «الكبرى» the second object of «لِنُرِيَك» and referred it to the nearer sign; and his statement has been weakened by [the fact] that the benefits of the staff are greater. This is not hidden." End of the quotation, in summary.

semin-durr:25-25.t: His saying: {لِي صَدْرِي}: «لي» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «اشرح». al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: what is the use of «لي» in His saying {اشرح لِي صَدْرِي وَيَسِّرْ لي أَمْرِي}, when the sense is complete without it? I say: He first made the speech vague, saying 'expand for me' and 'ease for me', so it was known that there is something expanded and something eased; then He clarified and removed the vagueness by mentioning them, so it was more emphatic for the request of expanding his breast and easing his affair."

semin-durr:26-26.t: One says: يَسَّرْتُه لكذا ("I made him ready for such-and-such"), and from it is {فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لليسرى} [al-Layl: 7]; and يَسَّرْتُ له كذا ("I made such-and-such easy for him"), and from it is this verse.

semin-durr:27-27.t: His saying: {مِّن لِّسَانِي}: it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted, as a naʿt (adjective) of «عُقْدَةً», i.e. "one of the knots of my tongue"; al-Zamakhsharī mentioned nothing else. It may also be attached to «احلُلْ» itself; the first is better.

semin-durr:29-29.t:
His saying: {واجعل لِّي وَزِيراً}: «لي» may be a second object placed first, with «وزيراً» as the first object. On this view «مِنْ أهلي» may be a naʿt (adjective) of «وزيراً», or it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to the making (al-jaʿl).
«هارونَ» is a badal (substitute) of «وزيراً». Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed «هارونَ» to be an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) of «وزيراً», and al-Zamakhsharī mentioned nothing else. When al-Shaykh reported this, he did not follow it with any objection, which is surprising of him; for ʿaṭf bayān requires agreement in definiteness and indefiniteness, and you know that «وزيراً» is indefinite and «هارونَ» definite. al-Zamakhsharī did the like previously in His saying: {فِيهِ آيَاتٌ بَيِّنَاتٌ مَّقَامُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ} [Āl ʿImrān: 97], and the discussion with him has already been given there, and it applies here again.
«هارونَ» may also be accusative by an omitted verb, as though He said: "I single out from among them Hārūn", i.e. from among my family. Or «وزيراً» may be the second object and «هارونَ» the first, the second having been placed before it out of concern for the matter of the ministry. On this view, His saying «لي» may be attached to the making itself, or attached to something omitted as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «وزيراً», since it was originally its adjective; and «مِنْ أهلي» is according to its two views stated above. Or «وزيراً» may be the first object and «مِنْ أهلي» the second, and His saying «لي» is like His saying {وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَّهُ كُفُواً أَحَدٌ} [al-Ikhlāṣ: 4] — they mean that the meaning is completed by it. Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned that. When al-Shaykh reported it, he did not follow it with any objection, and that is surprising; because the condition for the two objects in the chapter of the nawāsikh (abrogating governors) is that a nominal sentence can validly be formed [from them], and if you began with «وزير» and gave «من أهلي» as its predicate, it would not be permissible, since there is nothing to license beginning with it [an indefinite].
«أخي» is a badal or an ʿaṭf bayān of «هارونَ». al-Zamakhsharī said: "If it is made another ʿaṭf bayān, that is permissible and good." al-Shaykh said: "ʿAṭf bayān is unlikely in it, because in ʿaṭf bayān it is mostly the case that the first is less well-known than it, and this is the reverse." I say: al-Zamakhsharī did not mean that «أخي» is an ʿaṭf bayān of «هارون», so that al-Shaykh should say that the first, i.e. «هارون», is better known than the second, i.e. «أخي». al-Zamakhsharī only meant that it is also an ʿaṭf bayān of «وزيراً», and for that reason he said "another". His wording must be cited so that it is known he meant nothing but what I have stated. He said: "«وزيراً» and «هارونَ» are the two objects of His saying «اجعَلْ», or «لي وزيراً» are its two objects and «هارونَ» is an ʿaṭf bayān of the minister; and «أخي» in both views is a badal of «هارون»; and if it is made another ʿaṭf bayān, that is permissible and good."
So his saying "another" makes it certain that it is an ʿaṭf bayān of what he previously made [Hārūn] an ʿaṭf bayān of.
al-Zamakhsharī allowed «أخي» to be nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar (predicate) being the clause of His saying «اشْدُدْ به»; that is according to the majority's reading of it in the form of a supplication, and on this view the pause is on «هارونَ».
Ibn ʿĀmir read «أَشْدُدْ» with a fatḥa on the hamza of the imperfect prefix, the verb being jussive (majzūm) as the answer to the command, and «وأُشْرِكْهُ» with a ḍamma on the hamza of the imperfect prefix, the verb being jussive by conjunction with what precedes. The rest read with the connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) dropped from the first and the disjunctive hamza (hamzat al-qaṭʿ) with a fatḥa in the second, as both being a supplication by Mūsā to his Lord for that. On this reading the conjunction has been left out in this clause alone, unlike the clauses of supplication that preceded it.
al-Ḥasan read «أُشَدِّدُ», the imperfect of شَدَّد with doubling.
al-wazīr (the minister): it has been said that it is derived from al-wizr, which is weight; he was so called because he bears the burdens and costs of kingship, so he is a helper in the affair of the king and follows his command. It has also been said: rather it is from al-wazar, which is refuge, as in His saying: {لاَ وَزَرَ} [al-Qiyāma: 11]; and [the poet] said:
3287 - من السِّباع الضَّواري دونَه وَزَرٌ ... والناسُ شَرُّهُمُ ما دونَه وَزَرُ
كم مَعْشرٍ سَلِموا لم يُؤْذِهِمْ سَبُعٌ ... وما نرى بَشَراً لم يُؤْذِهِمْ بَشَرُ
(From the ravening beasts there is a refuge; but people's evil has no refuge against it. How many a company was safe, no beast harming them; yet we see no humans whom humans have not harmed.)
It has also been said: from al-muʾāzara, which is mutual help. al-Zamakhsharī transmitted that from al-Aṣmaʿī, and said: "The analogical form would have been أَزِير", meaning with hamza, because the root is so. al-Zamakhsharī said: "So the hamza was changed into wāw, and the reason for changing it into that is that the pattern faʿīl has come with the meaning of mufāʿil abundantly, as in their words ʿashīr, jalīs, khalīṭ, ṣadīq, khalīl and nadīm; so when it was changed in its sister [form] it was changed in it, and treating a thing like its counterpart is not rare; with regard also to يُوازِرُ and its sisters, and to al-muwāzara."
I say: he means that wazīr has the meaning of muwāzir, and in muwāzir the hamza is changed into wāw by a regular change, because it is a hamza with fatḥa after a ḍamma, so it is like «مُوَجَّل» and «يُوَاخذكم» and the like; so «أزير» was treated like it in the change, even though the cause of the change is not present in it.

semin-durr:33-33.t: His saying: {كَثِيراً}: a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of the maṣdar, as is the view of Sībawayh. Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed it to be a naʿt of an omitted [noun of] time, i.e. "a long time".

semin-durr:36-36.t: His saying: {سُؤْلَكَ}: the pattern fuʿl here has the meaning of mafʿūl (passive participle), as in ukl meaning maʾkūl (eaten) and khubr meaning makhbūr (known by experience). It is not by analogy.

semin-durr:37-37.t: «مرة» is a maṣdar (verbal noun). «أخرى» is the feminine of akhar meaning "other". Some claimed that it means ākhira ("last"), so that it would be the counterpart of "first", and devised a way for that by saying: "He called it 'another' although it is the first, because it is 'another' in mention."

semin-durr:38-38.t: His saying: {إِذْ أَوْحَيْنَآ}: the governor of «إذ» is «مَنَنَّا», i.e. "We conferred favour on you at the time We inspired [Translator's note: the source has «إلجائنا» ("Our compelling"), probably for «إيحائنا» ("Our inspiring").] your mother". The vagueness in His saying {مَا يوحى} is for magnification, like His saying: {فَغَشِيَهُمْ مِّنَ اليم مَا غَشِيَهُمْ} [Ṭā Hā: 78].

semin-durr:39-39.t:
His saying: {أَنِ اقذفيه}: «أنْ» may be explicative (mufassira), because inspiration has the meaning of saying; al-Zamakhsharī mentioned nothing else. Others allowed it to be maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya), in which case its position is accusative as a badal (substitute) of «ما يوحى». The pronouns in His saying {أَنِ اقذفيه} to its end refer to Mūsā (peace be upon him), because he is the one being spoken about. Some allowed the pronoun in His saying {فاقذفيه فِي اليم} to refer to the chest (al-tābūt), and what is after and before it to Mūsā (peace be upon him). al-Zamakhsharī faulted this and made it a disharmony, or something that takes the Quran out of its inimitability, for he said: "The pronouns all refer to Mūsā; having some of them refer to him and some to the chest is an ugliness, because of the disharmony of the composition (naẓm) it leads to. If you say: what was cast into the sea was the chest, and likewise what was thrown onto the shore — I say: what harm would it do you if you made what was cast and thrown onto the shore Mūsā inside the chest, so that the pronouns are not split and the composition becomes disharmonious for you — the composition which is the mother of the Quran's inimitability and the standard on which the challenge was made; and observing it is the most important duty of the exegete."
al-Shaykh said: "Someone might say: when a pronoun is fit to refer to the nearer and to the farther, its reference to the nearer is preferable, and the grammarians have stated this explicitly; so its reference to the chest in His saying {فاقذفيه فِي اليم فَلْيُلْقِهِ اليم} is preferable. The answer is: when one of the two is the one spoken about and the other a complement (faḍla), its reference to the one spoken about is preferable, and nearness is not taken into account. For this reason we refuted Abū Muḥammad Ibn Ḥazm in his claim that the pronoun in His saying {فَإِنَّهُ رِجْسٌ} [al-Anʿām: 145] refers to «خنزير», not to «لحم», because it is the nearest thing mentioned, so that its fat, cartilage, bone and skin would thereby be forbidden; for the thing spoken about is «لحمَ خنزيرٍ», not «خنزير»." I say: this question, and what people have said about it, has already been treated in al-Anʿām.

His saying: {فَلْيُلْقِهِ اليم}: this is a command whose meaning is a statement; but being a command in wording, its answer in His saying {يَأْخُذْهُ} was made jussive (majzūm). It came out in the form of a command only for emphasis, since the command is the most decisive and emphatic of verbs. al-Zamakhsharī said: "Since it was Allah's will and wish that the current of the sea's water should not fail to bring him to the shore and throw him onto it, He followed in that the way of figurative speech, and made the sea as though it possessed discernment, commanded to do that so that it would obey the command and comply with its prescription."
«بالساحل» may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted, the bāʾ being for the ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "being in contact with the shore"; or it may be attached to the verb itself, the bāʾ being locative, meaning «في».

His saying: {مِّنِّي}: there are two views on it. al-Zamakhsharī said: "It must be one of two: either it is attached to «أَلْقَيْتُ», so the meaning is 'in that I loved you, and whom Allah loves, hearts love'; or it is attached to something omitted that is an adjective of «محبةً», i.e. 'a love arising, or occurring, from Me, which I Myself have planted in the hearts and sown in them'."

His saying: {وَلِتُصْنَعَ}: the generality read it with a kasra on the lām, a ḍamma on the tāʾ and a fatḥa on the nūn, as a passive, the verb being accusative by an implied «أنْ» after the lām. There are two views on it. First: this cause is conjoined to an implied cause before it; the implied form is "so that you be treated gently, and so that you be made", or "so that [people] be tender towards you and you be cared for, and so that you be made". That implied cause is attached to His saying «وألقيتُ», i.e. "I cast love upon you so that [people] be tender towards you and so that you be made". So in reality it is attached to what precedes it, namely the casting of love.
Second: this lām is attached to something implied after it, its implied form being: "and so that you be made under My eye, I did that", or "such-and-such happened". The meaning of «لتُصْنَعَ» is: so that you be reared and treated well while I watch over you and observe you, as a person watches over a thing with his own eye when he takes care of it. al-Zamakhsharī said this.
al-Ḥasan and Abū Nahīk read «ولِتَصْنَعَ» with a fatḥa on the tāʾ. Thaʿlab said: "Its meaning is: so that your movement and your conduct be under an eye from Me." al-Zamakhsharī said something close to it. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "i.e. so that you do what I command you within My sight."
Abū Jaʿfar and Shayba read «ولْتُصْنَعْ» with a sukūn on the lām and the ʿayn and a ḍamma on the tāʾ; it is a command meaning: let him be reared and let him be treated well. It is reported from Abū Jaʿfar in this reading that the lām of command has a kasra. I say: with the kasra of the lām or its sukūn, in the case where the ʿayn is made quiescent, it may possibly be the lām of kay (purpose), made quiescent only by analogy with katf and kabd, and the verb accusative; and the quiescence of the ʿayn is for the sake of assimilation, and it is recited in continuous recitation only with assimilation.

semin-durr:40-40.t:
His saying: {إِذْ تمشي}: there are several views on the governor of this adverb. First: its governor is «ألقيتُ», i.e. "I cast upon you love from Me at the time your sister was walking".
Second: it is accusative by His saying «ولتُصْنَعَ», i.e. "so that you be reared and treated well at this time". al-Zamakhsharī said: "The governor of «إذ تشمي» [Translator's note: so in the source, for «إذ تمشي».] is «ألقيتُ» or «لتُصْنع»." Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«إذ تمشي» may be attached to either of the two verbs." I say: by the two verbs he means the preceding «ألقيتُ» or «لتُصْنَعَ». On this view the question may belong to the chapter of al-tanāzuʿ (contention of two governors), because each of these two governors seeks this adverb in terms of meaning, and it would be a case of giving government to the second, with omission from the first. This is only fully plausible if you make «ولِتُصْنَعَ» conjoined to an omitted cause attached to «أَلْقَيْتُ»; but if you make it attached to an implied verb after it, that becomes far-fetched or impossible, because the second has then become part of another clause.
Third: «إذ تمشي» is a badal (substitute) of «إذ أَوْحَيْنا». al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: how can the substitution be valid when the two times are different and far apart? I say: just as it is valid — even though the time is wide and its two ends far apart — for a man to say to you: 'I met so-and-so in such-and-such a year', and you say: 'And I met him then', though perhaps he met him at its beginning and you at its end." al-Shaykh said: "It is not as he mentioned, because the year admits of breadth, so their meeting occurred within it; unlike these two adverbs, for each of them is narrow, not broad, since they are specified by what they are annexed to. So the second cannot occur in the adverb in which the first occurred, since the first is not broad enough for the occurrence of the inspiration and of the sister's walking in it. The time of the verb's occurrence does not comprise parts in some of which the walking occurred, unlike the year." I say: this is a strained imposition on him by [al-Shaykh], for the time of meeting is also narrow and does not hold both their acts; that is only built on leniency, since what is meant is that the time comprises both their acts.
Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It may be a badal of the first «إذ», because his sister's walking was a favour to him." He means that His saying «إذ أَوْحَيْنا» is accusative by His saying «مَنَنَّا», so if «إذ تمشي» is made a badal of it, it too is a favour conferred upon him.
Fourth: its governor is implied, its implied form being "Remember when your sister was walking"; on this view it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), because the meaning would be corrupted on the adverbial reading.
The generality read «كي تَقَرَّ» with a fatḥa on the tāʾ and the qāf. A group read «تَقِرَّ» with a kasra on the qāf; it was stated in Sūrat Maryam that these are two dialects. Janāḥ ibn Ḥubaysh read «تُقَرُّ» with a ḍamma on the tāʾ and a fatḥa on the qāf, as a passive,
«عينُها» being nominative as the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).

His saying: {فُتُوناً}: there are two views on it. First: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) of the pattern fuʿūl, like al-quʿūd and al-julūs, except that fuʿūl is rare with transitive verbs; from it are al-shukūr, al-kufūr, al-thubūr and al-luzūm. The Exalted said: {لِّمَنْ أَرَادَ أَن يَذَّكَّرَ أَوْ أَرَادَ شُكُوراً} [al-Furqān: 62]. Second: it is the plural of fatn or of fitna, disregarding the feminine tāʾ, like «حُجُور» and «بُدُوْر» for ḥajra and badra; i.e. "We tried you with various kinds of trials". From Ibn ʿAbbās: he was born in a year in which the male infants were being killed; his mother cast him into the sea; he killed the Copt; he hired himself out for ten years; he lost his way; and his flock scattered on a dark night. When Saʿīd ibn Jubayr asked him about that, he answered him with what I have mentioned, and kept saying at each one: "This is a trial, O Ibn Jubayr." al-Zamakhsharī said its meaning. Others said: with kinds of trials (futūn) among the fitan, i.e. ordeals with which you are tested.

His saying: {على قَدَرٍ}: attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted, as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «جئت», i.e. "you came in accordance with what was decreed for you". So Abū al-Baqāʾ implied it, and that is an explanation of meaning. The technical (grammatical) explanation is: then you came, being settled or being upon a fixed measure; as in the saying of the other [poet]:
3288 - نال الخلافةَ أو جاءَتْ على قَدَرٍ ... كما أتى رَبَّه موسى على قَدَرِ
(He attained the caliphate — or rather it came by decree — just as Mūsā came to his Lord by decree.)

semin-durr:41-41.t: The meaning of «اصْطَنَعْتُكَ» is "I made you pure (i.e. devoted)", and "I chose you"; it is of the pattern iftiʿāl from al-ṣunʿ (making), the tāʾ having been changed to ṭāʾ because of the elevated letter (ḥarf al-istiʿlāʾ). This is a figurative expression for the nearness of his rank and his closeness to his Lord; because one does not "make for oneself" (yaṣṭaniʿu) anyone except one whom one chooses.

semin-durr:42-42.t:
His saying: {وَلاَ تَنِيَا}: one says: ونى يَني وَنْياً, like وَعَدَ يَعِد وَعْداً, when one slackens . . . al-wany is slackness. From it is "a woman who is anāt", whom they described with slowness in rising, as an allusion to her stoutness. [The poet] said:
3289 - مِنَّا الأَناةُ وبعضُ القومِ يَحْسَبُنا ... أَنَّا بِطاءٌ وفي إبطائِنا سَرَعُ
(Deliberateness is ours, and some people reckon us slow — yet in our slowness there is speed.)
The original is wanāt; they substituted the hamza for the wāw, as in aḥad for waḥad, and it is not by analogy. In the ḥadīth: "In you are two traits that Allah loves: forbearance and deliberateness (al-anāt)."
al-wānī is one who falls short in his affair. The poet said:
3290 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... فما أنا بالواني ولا الضِّرَعِ الغُمْرِ
(... I am neither a slacker nor a weak, inexperienced man.)
ونى is an intransitive verb that does not take an object. Some claimed that it may be one of the sisters of زَال and انفك, so that, on condition of negation or something resembling it, it operates as kāna operates, and one says: «ما وَنى زيدٌ قائماً», i.e. "Zayd did not cease standing". al-Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn Ibn Mālik cited as evidence for that the poet's saying:
3291 - لا يَنِيْ الحُبُّ شِيْمةَ الحِبِّ ما دا ... مَ فلا تَحْسَبَنَّه ذا ارْعِواءِ
(Love does not cease to be the trait of the lover as long as it lasts, so do not think it will desist.)
i.e. al-ḥubb (with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ: love) does not cease to be the trait of al-ḥibb (with kasra: the lover). Those who reject that interpret the verse as having an omitted preposition; for this verb is made transitive sometimes with «عَنْ» and sometimes with «في»: one says "I did not slacken from your need" or "in your need". So the implied form is: "love does not slacken in the trait of the lover", and there is an eloquent figure in it. In the noble verse it has been made transitive with «في».
Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read «ولا تِنِيا» with a kasra on the tāʾ, in harmony with the vowel of the nūn. And he made the yāʾ of «ذِكْرِيْ» quiescent . . . . . . .

semin-durr:43-43.t: He mentioned the one gone to in His saying {اذهبآ إلى فِرْعَوْنَ} and omitted it in the first, in His saying {اذهب أَنتَ وَأَخُوكَ}, for brevity of speech. It has also been said: they were first commanded to go to people in general, and then secondly to Pharaoh in particular. There is remoteness in that [Translator's note: the source repeats the phrase "to Pharaoh in particular, and there is remoteness in that; rather the two goings are directed to one thing" twice; it is translated once.]; rather the two goings are directed to one thing, namely Pharaoh. He omitted from each of the two goings what He stated in the other: He omitted the one gone to from the first and stated it in the second, and omitted what they were to go with, namely «بآياتي», from the second and stated it in the first.

semin-durr:44-44.t:
Abū Muʿādh read «قولاً لَيْناً», which is a lightening of layyin, like mayt for mayyit.
His saying: {لَّعَلَّهُ}: there are several views on it. First: «لعلَّ» has its proper sense of hope; that is in relation to those sent, namely Mūsā and Hārūn, i.e. "go upon your hope and your aspiration for his faith; go hoping and aspiring". This is the meaning of al-Zamakhsharī's statement; it cannot properly apply to Allah the Exalted, since He knows the outcomes of affairs. From Sībawayh: "Every «لعلَّ» and «عسى» that occurs in the Quran is, from Allah, certain" — meaning that it is impossible for its [literal] meaning to remain in respect of Allah the Exalted. Second: «لعلَّ» means «كي», so it conveys cause.
This is the view of al-Farrāʾ, who said: "As you say: 'Work, that you may (laʿallaka) take your wage', i.e. so that you take." Third: it is interrogative, i.e. "will he take heed or fear?" This is a fallen view, because interrogation is impossible in respect of Allah the Exalted, just as hope is impossible. So since interpretation is unavoidable, keeping the word upon what it denotes is better than taking it out of it.

semin-durr:45-45.t:
His saying: {أَن يَفْرُطَ}: «أَنْ يَفْرُطَ» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «نخاف». One says: فَرَطَ يَفْرُط meaning "he went ahead and preceded"; from it is al-fāriṭ, the one who goes ahead of those coming down to the water; and a horse that is faraṭ outstrips the horses. I.e. "we fear that he will hasten punishment against us and rush us with it" — al-Zamakhsharī said this. An instance of al-fāriṭ meaning the one who goes ahead of the water-comers is the poet's saying:
3292 - واسْتعجلونا وكانوا مِنْ صحابَتنا ... كما تَقَدَّم فُرَّاطُ لوُرَّادِ
(They hastened ahead of us, though they were of our company, as the forerunners go ahead of those coming to water.)
In the ḥadīth: "I am your faraṭ at the Pool", i.e. the one who goes ahead of you and precedes you.
Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, Ibn Muḥayṣin and Abū Nawfal read «يُفْرَط» with a ḍamma on the imperfect prefix and a fatḥa on the rāʾ, as a passive. The meaning is: they feared that he would be driven ahead into punishment, i.e. that something would drive him to it and to hastening it: either his people, or love of leadership, or his claim to divinity.
Ibn Muḥayṣin in one transmission and al-Zaʿfarānī read «أَن يُفَرِّطَ» [Translator's note: so vocalised in the source, but the description "from أفرط" points to «يُفْرِطَ».] with a ḍamma on the imperfect prefix and a kasra on the rāʾ, from أفرط. al-Zamakhsharī said: "From 'someone else afraṭahu' when he drove him to haste; they feared that something would drive him to hastening punishment." Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr said:
3293 - تَنْفِي الرياحُ القذى عنه وأَفْرَطَه ... مِنْ صَوْبِ ساريةٍ بِيْضٌ يَعالِيْلُ
(The winds sweep the motes away from it, and white successive clouds of a night-rain's downpour have filled it ahead.)
i.e. these white [clouds] hastened to it to fill it. The fāʿil (agent) of «يَفْرُطَ» is the pronoun of Pharaoh; this is the apparent sense, from which one should not deviate. Abū al-Baqāʾ made it implied because the speech indicates it, saying: "The implied form may be: 'that a word from him should rush out against us', the word having been implied because the context indicates it, as you say 'a word rushed out of me'; or the fāʿil may be the pronoun of Pharaoh, as it is in «يطغى»."

semin-durr:46-46.t: The object of {أَسْمَعُ وأرى} is omitted. It has been said that its implied form is: "I hear your words and see your deeds". From Ibn ʿAbbās: "I hear his answer to you and see what he does with you." Or it may be omission for restriction (ḥadhf al-iqtiṣār), as in: {يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ} [Āl ʿImrān: 156].

semin-durr:47-47.t:
His saying: {قَدْ جِئْنَاكَ بِآيَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّكَ}: al-Zamakhsharī said: this clause stands, in relation to the first clause, namely {إِنَّا رَسُولاَ رَبِّكَ}, in the place of clarification and explanation; because the claim of messengership is established only by its proof, which is the coming of the sign. «آية» was made singular and not dual, though he had two signs with him, only because what is meant in this place is establishing the claim by its proof; so it is as though it were said: "We have come to you with a miracle, a proof and an argument for what we have claimed of messengership". Likewise He said: {قَدْ جِئْتُكُمْ بِبَيِّنَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ} [al-Aʿrāf: 105], {فَأْتِ بِآيَةٍ إِن كُنتَ مِنَ الصادقين} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 154], {أَوَلَوْ جِئْتُكَ بِشَيءٍ مُّبِينٍ} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 30].
{على مَنِ اتبع الهدى}: it may be something they were commanded to say, so that it is in the position of accusative, as though it were said: "so say also: and peace be upon whoever follows guidance". Or it may be a greeting from the two of them that they were not commanded to say, so the clause is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position. Some claimed that «على» has the meaning of the lām, i.e. "and peace be to whoever follows guidance"; there is no need for this.

semin-durr:48-48.t: His saying: {أَنَّ العذاب على مَن كَذَّبَ}: «أنَّ» and what is within its scope are in the position of nominative, because they stand in place of the fāʿil (agent) that was omitted in {أُوحِيَ إِلَيْنَآ}. The reason for making it passive is fear that Pharaoh might let slip something rash against the One who inspired, had they named Him; so they folded away mention of Him out of reverence for Him and disdain for the one addressed.

semin-durr:49-49.t: His saying: {ياموسى}: he called Mūsā alone after addressing the two of them together: either because Mūsā is the principal in the messengership, and Hārūn a follower, a support and a minister; or because Pharaoh, in his malice, knew of the impediment in Mūsā's tongue and knew of his brother's eloquence, as evidenced by His saying {وَأَخِي هَارُونُ هُوَ أَفْصَحُ مِنِّي لِسَاناً} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 34] and His saying {وَلاَ يَكَادُ يُبِينُ} [al-Zukhruf: 52], so he wanted to make him speak rather than his brother; or because the conjoined (maʿṭūf) [name] was omitted since it is known, i.e. "O Mūsā and Hārūn". Abū al-Baqāʾ said this, and began with it; but there is no need for it. It might be said: what made the omission good is that «موسى» is a verse-end (fāṣila). It is not to be said: it would have sufficed for that to put Hārūn first and Mūsā last, saying "O Hārūn and Mūsā", so that the correspondence of verse-ends is obtained without omission — because beginning with Mūsā is more important, so he is the one begun with.

semin-durr:50-50.t:
His saying: {أعطى كُلَّ شَيءٍ خَلْقَهُ}: there are two views on this verse. First: «كلَّ شيءٍ» is the first object and «خَلْقَه» the second object, with the meaning: He gave every thing its form and shape that matches the benefit attached to it — as He gave the eye the configuration that matches seeing, and the ear the shape that matches and suits hearing, and likewise the hand, the foot and the tongue; or He gave every animal its counterpart in creation and form, making the stallion and the mare a pair, the she-camel and the he-camel, the man and the woman, and none of them is paired with other than its own kind, nor with what differs from its own make. It has also been said: the meaning is "He gave every created thing its creation", i.e. He is the one who originated it. It has also been said: the meaning is "He gave every thing He created its make and its form, with the perfection that suits it; He did not make the creation of man in the creation of beasts, nor the reverse; rather He created every thing and determined it with exact determination".
Second: «كلَّ شيءٍ» is the second object and «خَلْقَه» the first, the second having been placed before it; the meaning is: He gave His creatures every thing they need and make use of.
ʿAbd Allāh [Ibn Masʿūd], al-Ḥasan, al-Aʿmash, Abū Nahīk, Ibn Abī Isḥāq, Nuṣayr from al-Kisāʾī, and some of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ read «خَلَقَه» with a fatḥa on the lām, as a past verb. In this reading the clause may be in the position of accusative as an adjective of «كل», or in the position of genitive as an adjective of «شيء»; this is the meaning of al-Zamakhsharī's statement: "an adjective of the muḍāf", meaning «كل», "or of the muḍāf ilayhi", meaning «شيءٍ». The second object on this reading is omitted. Its omission may be omission for brevity (ḥadhf ikhtiṣār), because there is indication of it, i.e. "He gave every thing He created what it needs and what sets it right, or its perfection"; or its omission may be omission for restriction (ḥadhf iqtiṣār), the meaning being: every thing Allah created, He did not leave it devoid of His bounty and His giving.

semin-durr:51-51.t: al-bāl is thought. One says: "such-and-such occurred to his bāl (mind)". It is not put in the dual or plural, and its plural «بالات» is anomalous. It is also said of a matter that is cared about; hence one says: «ما بالَيْتُ بالةً» ("I paid it no heed at all"), and the original is . . . . . . , its final radical having been dropped for lightness.

semin-durr:52-52.t:
His saying: {قَالَ عِلْمُهَا عِندَ رَبِّي}: there are several views on the khabar (predicate) of this mubtadaʾ (subject). First: it is «عند ربي»; on this view His saying «في كتاب» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the [notion of] being-settled to which the adverb is attached; or it is attached to something omitted, as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in the adverb; or it is a second khabar.
Second: the khabar is His saying «في كتاب»; on this view His saying «عند ربي» is governed by the being-settled to which «في كتاب» is attached, as stated above in the reverse case; or it is a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in the preposition-phrase that serves as khabar. There is disagreement on this, I mean placing the ḥāl before its abstract (maʿnawī) governor. al-Akhfash allows it and adduces as evidence the reading {والسماوات مَطْوِيَّاتٍ بِيَمِينِهِ} [al-Zumar: 67] and [the poet's] saying:
3294 - رَهْطُ ابنِ كوزٍ مُحقِبيْ أَدْراعِهمْ ... فيهم ورَهْطُ رَبيعةَ بنِ حُذارِ
(The clan of Ibn Kūz, with their coats of mail strapped behind them, are among them, and the clan of Rabīʿa ibn Ḥudhār.)
Some grammarians said: when the governor is abstract and the ḥāl is an adverb or its equivalent, placing it first is good according to al-Akhfash and others, and this is a case of it. Or it may be an adverb of the knowledge itself; or it may be a ḥāl from the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive), which is the pronoun in «عليها» [Translator's note: so in the source; the pronoun is in «عِلْمُها».]. «في كتاب» may not be attached to «عِلْمها» on our view that «عند ربي» is the khabar — as «عند» could be attached to it — lest it entail separating the maṣdar (verbal noun) from what it governs by something foreign; it has already been stated that one does not give a predicate for a relative noun until its ṣila (relative clause) is complete.
Third: the adverb and the preposition together form a single khabar in meaning, so it would be like «هذا حُلْوٌ حامِض» ("this is sweet-sour"). Abū al-Baqāʾ said this, and it is open to question, since each of them is independent in conveying a predicative benefit, unlike «هذا حلو حامِضٌ».
On the pronoun in «عِلْمُها» there are two views. The more apparent: it refers to the generations (al-qurūn). The second: it refers to the Resurrection (al-qiyāma), because the mention of the generations indicates that; for he asked him about the raising of the nations, and the raising indicates the Resurrection.

His saying: {لاَّ يَضِلُّ رَبِّي}: there are two views on this clause. First: it is in the position of genitive as an adjective of «كتاب», with the returning pronoun omitted, its implied form being: "in a book that my Lord does not lose", or "whose keeping my Lord does not lose"; so «ربي» is the fāʿil (agent) of «يَضِلُّ» on this implied form. It has also been said that its implied form is: "[the book does not miss] my Lord" [Translator's note: the source has «الكتابَ ربي», evidently a corrupted phrase.]; so in «يَضِلُّ» there is a pronoun referring to «كتاب», and «ربي» is accusative by way of reverence (ʿalā al-taʿẓīm), the original being "from my Lord", the preposition having been dropped by extension of usage. One says: ضَلَلْتُ كذا and ضَلِلْتُه, with a fatḥa and a kasra on the lām — two well-known dialects, the better known of them being the fatḥa. Second: it is a resumptive clause with no grammatical position, which Allah, blessed and exalted is He, brought simply to give information about that, reporting from Mūsā.
al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, al-Jaḥdarī, ʿĪsā al-Thaqafī, Ibn Muḥayṣin and Ḥammād ibn Salama read «لا يُضِلُّ» with a ḍamma on the yāʾ, i.e. my Lord does not lose the book, i.e. does not let it go to waste; one says: أَضْلَلْتُ الشيءَ, i.e. I lost it.
So «ربي» is the fāʿil on this implied form. It has also been said that its implied form is: "no one makes my Lord miss His knowledge", i.e. the knowledge of the book, so «الربّ» is accusative by way of reverence.
Some distinguished between ضَلَلْتُ and أَضْلَلْت, saying: «ضَلَلْتُ منزلي» ("I could not find my house"), without alif, but «أَضْلَلْت بعيري» ("I lost my camel") and the like for animals, with the alif. al-Rummānī transmitted that from the Arabs. al-Farrāʾ said: "One says ضَلَلْتُ الشيءَ — and ضَلِلْتُ, two dialects — when you mistake its place and are not guided to it, as in your saying 'I lost the road and the house'; and one does not say أَضْلَلْتُه except when it is lost from you, like a riding animal that got loose, and the like."

His saying: {وَلاَ ينسى}: there are two views on the fāʿil of «ينسى». First: it refers to «ربي», i.e. "and my Lord does not forget what He has recorded in the book". Second: the fāʿil is a pronoun referring to the book, figuratively, just as enumeration is attributed to it figuratively in His saying {إِلاَّ أَحْصَاهَا} [al-Kahf: 49], since it is the locus of enumeration.

semin-durr:53-53.t:
His saying: {الذي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ}: there are two views on this relative noun. First: it is the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), or accusative by an implied «أمدح» ("I praise"); on both these implied forms it is from the speech of Allah the Exalted, not from the speech of Mūsā. We needed that only because His saying {فَأَخْرَجْنَا بِهِ}, His saying {كُلُواْ وارعوا أَنْعَامَكُمْ} and His saying {مِنْهَا خَلَقْنَاكُمْ} up to His saying {وَلَقَدْ أَرَيْنَاهُ} cannot be from the speech of Mūsā; therefore we made it from the speech of the Creator, exalted is He. There is in it then a shift (iltifāt) from the third-person pronoun to the pronoun of the speaker magnifying Himself. If you say: I make it from the speech of Mūsā — meaning that he described his Lord, exalted is He, thus and then shifted to informing about Allah in the first-person wording — it is said: we made it a shift in the first view only because the speaker is one, unlike this; for the shift mentioned cannot apply in it, nor in its sisters, from the speech of Allah.
Second: «الذي» is an adjective of «ربي», so it is in the position of nominative or accusative according to the parsing of «ربي» given above. It contains the difficulty mentioned above in the arrangement of the speech, from His saying «فأَخْرَجْنا» and its sisters, namely the impermissibility of the shift, even though al-Zamakhsharī and al-Ḥūfī held that [view]. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Mūsā's speech ended at His saying {وَأَنزَلَ مِنَ السمآء مَآءً}, and His saying «فأخرَجْنا» to the end is from the speech of Allah the Exalted"; there is remoteness in that.
The Kufans read «مَهْداً» with a fatḥa on the mīm and a sukūn on the hāʾ, without alif; the rest «مِهاداً» with a kasra on the mīm, a fatḥa on the hāʾ and an alif after it. There are two views on it. First: they are two maṣdars (verbal nouns) with one meaning; one says: مَهَدْتُه مَهْداً ومِهاداً. Second: they differ: mihād is the noun and mahd is the act; or mihād is the plural of mahd, like farkh and firākh, kaʿb and kiʿāb. Describing the earth as a mahd (cradle) is either for intensification, or by omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "possessing a cradle".

His saying: {شتى}: «شَتَّى» is of the pattern faʿlā, and its alif is for the feminine. It is the plural of shatīt, like marḍā as the plural of marīḍ, jarḥā as the plural of jarīḥ, and qatlā as the plural of qatīl. One says: شَتَّ الأمرُ يَشِتُّ شَتَّاً وشَتاتاً, so it is shatt, i.e. it was dispersed. shattān is a verbal noun (ism fiʿl) of the past meaning "they differed", and for that reason one [subject] does not suffice with it.
On «شَتَّى» there are several views. First: it is accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of «أَزْواجاً», i.e. "diverse pairs", meaning differing in colours and tastes. Second: it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «أزواجاً»; a ḥāl from an indefinite is permitted because it is specified by the adjective, namely «مِنْ نبات». Third: it is accusative as a ḥāl, also, from the fāʿil of the preposition-phrase; because when it occurs as an adjective it raises a pronoun as its fāʿil. Fourth: it is in the position of genitive as an adjective of «نبات». al-Zamakhsharī said: "It may be an adjective of «نبات», «نبات» being a maṣdar used as a name for what grows, as al-nabt is so used, so the singular and the plural are equal in it; meaning that they are diverse, differing in benefit, taste, colour, smell and shape, some of them suiting people and some suiting beasts." Abū al-Baqāʾ agreed with him too. But the apparent view is the first.

semin-durr:54-54.t:
His saying: {كُلُواْ}: [it is] in the accusative position by an omitted [verb of] saying, and that saying is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «أَخْرَجْنا», its implied form being: "So We brought forth such-and-such, saying: eat". The object of eating has been left out, in the manner of its omission in His saying: {كُلُواْ واشربوا} [al-Baqara: 60].
«وارْعَوْا»: رعى may be intransitive or transitive. One says: رعى دابَّته رَعْياً ("he pastured his beast"), so he is its pastor (rāʿī); and رَعَتِ الدابَّةُ ترعى رَعْياً ("the beast grazed"), so it is grazing (rāʿiya). In the verse it has come as transitive.
On al-nuhā there are two views. First: it is the plural of nuhya, like ghuraf as the plural of ghurfa. Second: it is a singular noun, a maṣdar (verbal noun) like al-hudā and al-surā; Abū ʿAlī said this. I had stated earlier, at the first of these places, that they said no maṣdar of the pattern fuʿal occurs from a verb with a weak final radical except surā, hudā and bukā, and that some added «لقى», and I cited a verse for it there; and this is another word, so it would be a fifth. al-nuhā is reason (al-ʿaql). They said: it was so called because it forbids (yanhā) its possessor from committing ugly deeds.

semin-durr:56-56.t:
His saying: {أَرَيْنَاهُ آيَاتِنَا}: it is from visual «رأى»; when the hamza of transfer entered it, it became transitive by it to two [objects], the first being the hāʾ and the second «آياتِنا». The meaning is: "We caused him to see". The annexation here stands in place of the definiteness of prior reference (al-taʿrīf al-ʿahdī), i.e. the well-known signs, such as the staff, the hand and the like; otherwise Allah the Exalted did not show Pharaoh all His signs. al-Zamakhsharī allowed the signs to be meant in general, in the sense "that Mūsā (peace be upon him) showed him the signs with which he was sent and enumerated to him the signs which the messengers before him (peace be upon them) brought; and he is a truthful prophet, so there is no difference between what he reports and what is witnessed."
al-Shaykh said: "There is remoteness in that, because informing of a thing is not called seeing it except by a remote figure. It has also been said: rather the seeing here is a seeing of the heart, so the meaning is 'We made him know'." And he supported that [Translator's note: the source does not make clear who "he" is.] by [the point] that he had shown him only the hand and the staff. Whoever allows using a word in its literal and its figurative sense [at once], or applying a homonym in both its meanings, allows both meanings together to be meant. Its emphasising the signs with «كلَّها» indicates that generality is meant, because they said: the benefit of tawkīd (emphasis) with «كل» and its sisters is to remove the misapprehension that the more specific has been put in place of the more general; so it is not to be claimed that by the signs He meant specific signs. This works on [the view] that the seeing is of the heart, and that by the signs is meant what indicates the oneness of Allah and the truthfulness of the conveyor. He did not mention the object of denying and refusing, out of magnifying it, and it is known.
[Translator's note: «معفولَ» in the source is a misprint for «مفعولَ» (object).]

semin-durr:58-58.t:
His saying: {فَلَنَأْتِيَنَّكَ}: the answer to an omitted oath, its implied form being: "By Allah, we shall surely bring you". His saying «بسِحْرٍ» may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to the bringing, and this is the apparent view; or it may be attached to something omitted, as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of the bringing, i.e. "being furnished with magic".

His saying: {مَوْعِداً}: it may be [a noun of] time, and His saying {مَوْعِدُكُمْ يَوْمُ الزينة} makes this preferable; the meaning is: "appoint for us a time of meeting", and for that reason he answered them with His saying {مَوْعِدُكُمْ يَوْمُ الزينة}. They weakened this on the ground that His saying {مَوْعِدُكُمْ يَوْمُ} [Translator's note: so in the source; from the context, «مَكَاناً سُوًى» is evidently meant.] is incompatible with it, and by His saying {لاَّ نُخْلِفُهُ}. He [the proponent] answered regarding His saying {لاَّ نُخْلِفُهُ} that the meaning is: "we will not break the time of meeting". It may be [a noun of] place; the meaning is: "make clear to us a known place that we and you know" . . . and it is supported by His saying {مَكَاناً سُوًى}. He said: this indicates that it is a place; but His saying {مَوْعِدُكُمْ يَوْمُ الزينة} is incompatible with it.
It may also be a maṣdar (verbal noun), and His saying {لاَّ نُخْلِفُهُ نَحْنُ وَلاَ أَنتَ} supports this, because an appointment is described as being broken or not. A group inclined to this, choosing it. It was objected to them by His saying {مَوْعِدُكُمْ يَوْمُ الزينة}, since it does not match it.
al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you make it a time, considering that His saying {مَوْعِدُكُمْ يَوْمُ الزينة} matches it, two things follow for you: that you make the time something broken, and that the governor of «مكاناً» becomes difficult for you. If you make it a place, because of His saying {مَكَاناً سُوى}, it also follows for you that you apply breaking to the place, and that His saying 'your appointment is the day of adornment' does not match it. The reading of al-Ḥasan does not match it as either time or place, because he read «يومَ الزينة» in the accusative. So it remains that it is made a maṣdar meaning 'promise', and an omitted muḍāf is implied, i.e. 'the place of the promise', and the pronoun in «نُخلِفُه» is made to refer to the appointment, and «مكاناً» is a badal (substitute) of the omitted 'place'. If you say: then how does His saying {مَوْعِدُكُمْ يَوْمُ الزينة} match it, when you must make it a time, while the question is about the place, not about the time? I say: it matches in meaning, even if it does not match in wording; because they had to gather on the day of adornment in a particular place well known for their gathering in it at that time; so by mentioning the time the place is known. As for the reading of al-Ḥasan, the appointment in it is a maṣdar and nothing else, and the meaning is: 'the fulfilment of your promise is on the day of adornment'; and this too matches by way of meaning. It is also possible not to imply an omitted muḍāf, the meaning being: 'set between us and you a promise that we will not break'."
Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is here a maṣdar, because of His saying {لاَّ نُخْلِفُهُ نَحْنُ وَلاَ أَنتَ}."
The making (al-jaʿl) here means rendering (al-taṣyīr); «مَوْعِداً» is the first object and the adverb is the second. The clause of His saying «لا نُخْلِفُه» is an adjective of «موعداً». «نحن» is a tawkīd (emphasis) that validates the conjunction with the latent nominative pronoun in «نُخْلفه». «مكاناً» is a badal of the omitted "place", as al-Zamakhsharī established. Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī and Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed «مكاناً» to be accusative as the second object of «اجعَلْ». He said: "On this view «موعداً» is also a place; and it is not accusative by «موعد», because it is a maṣdar that has been qualified." He means that its being accusative as a second object is valid, but on condition that the appointment has the meaning of place, so that the mubtadaʾ and the khabar in the underlying [sentence] match.
His saying "and it is not accusative by the maṣdar" means that one may not claim that «مكاناً» is accusative by «موعد», what is meant by «الموعد» being the maṣdar — even though it is permissible in terms of meaning — because the grammatical craft rejects it, namely [because of] the qualification of the maṣdar; and a condition for a maṣdar's governing is, according to the majority, that it not be qualified before governing.
This, which al-Fārisī and Abū al-Baqāʾ forbade, al-Zamakhsharī allowed and began with, saying: "If you say: by what is «مكاناً» made accusative? I say: by the maṣdar, or by what the maṣdar indicates. If you say: how does the answer match it? I say: on the reading of al-Ḥasan it is clear; on the reading of the generality it is on the implied form: 'your promise is the promise of the day of adornment'."
al-Shaykh said: "His saying that «مكاناً» is accusative by the maṣdar is not permissible, because it has been qualified before governing, by His saying «لا نُخْلِفُه», and it is [like] a relative; and a maṣdar, when qualified before governing, may not govern according to them." I say: adverbs and prepositional phrases are allowed latitude that is not allowed in other things. There is a well-known disagreement on the question, and Abū al-Qāsim [al-Zamakhsharī] inclined to allowing it.
al-Ḥūfī made «مكاناً» accusative as an adverb, its being accusative by «اجعل». So five views result for the accusative of «مكاناً». First: it is a badal of the omitted «مكاناً». Second: it is the second object of the making. Third: it is made accusative by an implied verb. Fourth: it is accusative by the maṣdar itself. Fifth: it is accusative as an adverb by «اجْعَلْ» itself.
Abū Jaʿfar and Shayba read «لا نُخْلِفْه» in the jussive (majzūm), as the answer to the command; the generality [read it] in the nominative, as an adjective of «مَوْعِد», as stated above.
Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamza, ʿĀṣim and al-Ḥasan read «سُوَىً» with a ḍamma on the sīn, with tanwīn in continuous recitation; the rest with a kasra on it. The kasra and the ḍamma are on [the view] that it is an adjective meaning "a fair place", except that adjectives of the pattern fuʿal are many, such as lubad and ḥuṭam, and of the pattern fiʿal few; Sībawayh reported «لحم زِيَم». al-Ḥasan did not give «سوى» tanwīn, treating continuous recitation like the pause. It cannot be that he made it a diptote because of deflection (al-ʿadl) to the pattern fuʿal, like ʿUmar, because that is in proper names; fuʿal in adjectives is declined fully, such as ḥuṭam and lubad.
ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read «سِوى» with a kasra, without tanwīn; it is like al-Ḥasan's reading in interpretation.
«سوى» means "fairness and equity". al-Fārisī said: "As though he said: its nearness to you is its nearness to us." al-Akhfash said: "«سوى» is short-vowelled (maqṣūr) if you give its sīn a kasra or a ḍamma, and long-vowelled (mamdūd) if you give it a fatḥa — three dialects — and in all of them it may mean 'other than', and 'fair' and 'midway between the two parties'." The poet said:
3295 - وإنَّ أبانا كان حَلَّ ببلدةٍ ... سِوَىً بين قَيْسٍ قيسِ عَيْلانَ والفِزْرِ
(Our father had settled in a land midway between Qays — Qays ʿAylān — and al-Fizr.)
He said: "And you say: 'I passed by a man siwāka, suwāka and sawāʾika', i.e. other than you; and it is used for all [numbers]." The highest of these dialects is the kasra; al-Naḥḥās said this. Some lexicographers and exegetes claimed that the meaning of «مكاناً سوى» is a level piece of ground, with no ruggedness or roughness in it.

semin-durr:59-59.t:
His saying: {مَوْعِدُكُمْ يَوْمُ الزينة}: the generality [read] «يومُ الزينة» in the nominative, as the khabar (predicate) of «موعدُكم». If you make «موعدكم» a time, you do not need to omit a muḍāf, since the implied form is "the time of the appointment is the day of adornment"; if you make it a maṣdar (verbal noun), you need to omit a muḍāf, its implied form being "your promise is the promise of the day of adornment".
al-Ḥasan, al-Aʿmash, ʿĪsā, ʿĀṣim in some of his transmissions, Abū Ḥaywa, Ibn Abī ʿAbla, Qatāda, al-Jaḥdarī and Hubayra read «يومَ» in the accusative. There are several views on it. First: it is the khabar of «موعدكم», on [the view] that by «الموعد» the maṣdar is meant, i.e. "your promise is occurring on the day of adornment", as in your saying: "the fighting is on such-and-such a day" and "the journey is tomorrow".
Second: «موعدُكم» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), by which the time is meant, and «ضُحَى» is its khabar, with definiteness intended in it, because it is the forenoon of that very day; al-Zamakhsharī said this. He did not make clear what governs the accusative of «يومَ الزينة»; it cannot be made accusative by «موعدُكم» on this implied form, because a mafʿil meaning time or place does not govern, even though it is derived; so its governor would be an implied verb. al-Shaykh took him to task over his saying "with definiteness intended", saying: "Because even though it is the forenoon of that very day, definiteness is not intended in it; rather it is indefinite, even if it belongs to a particular day; because it is neither deflected from the alif and lām, like saḥar, nor made definite by annexation. If you said «جئت يوم الجمعة بَكَراً» ('I came on Friday early'), we would not claim that «بَكَراً» is definite, even though you know that it belongs to a particular day."
Third: «موعدُكم» is a mubtadaʾ by which the maṣdar is meant, and «يومَ الزينةِ» is an adverb for it, and «ضحى» is accusative as an adverb, as the khabar of «الموعد», just as in the first view «يوم الزينة» was given as its predicate, as in: "the fighting is on such-and-such a day".

His saying: {وَأَن يُحْشَرَ}: there are two views on its position. First: genitive, by conjunction with «الزينة», i.e. "your appointment is the day of adornment and the day that [the people] are gathered", i.e. the day of the gathering of the people. Second: nominative, by conjunction with «يومُ»; the implied form is: "your appointment is such-and-such a day, and your appointment is that the people be gathered", i.e. their gathering.
Ibn Masʿūd, al-Jaḥdarī, Abū Nahīk and ʿAmr ibn Fāʾid read «وأن تَحْشُرَ الناسَ», with the tāʾ of address in «تَحْشُرَ»; it is also reported from them «يَحْشُرَ» with the yāʾ of the third person. «الناسَ» is accusative in both readings as the object. The pronoun in both readings is for Pharaoh, i.e. "and that you, O Pharaoh, gather", or "and that Pharaoh gather". Some allowed the fāʿil (agent) to be the pronoun of the day in the third-person reading; that is figurative: since the gathering occurs in it, it is attributed to it, as in: "his day is fasting and his night is standing [in prayer]".
«ضُحَىً» is accusative as an adverb, its governor being «يُحْشَر»; it is treated as masculine and feminine. al-ḍaḥāʾ, with the long vowel and a fatḥa on the ḍād, is later than al-ḍuḥā; because al-ḍuḥā is the rising of the day, and al-ḍaḥāʾ is after that, and it is masculine only.

semin-durr:60-60.t: His saying: {كَيْدَهُ}: there is the omission of a muḍāf in it, i.e. "the people of his plot".

semin-durr:61-61.t:
His saying: {فَيُسْحِتَكُم}: the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] and Ḥafṣ from ʿIṣām [Translator's note: so in the source, for ʿĀṣim.] read «فيُسْحِتَكم» with a ḍamma on the yāʾ and a kasra on the ḥāʾ; the rest with a fatḥa on both. The reading of the two brothers is from the four-letter أسْحَتَ, which is the dialect of Najd and Tamīm. al-Farazdaq al-Tamīmī said:
3296 - وعَضُّ زمانٍ يا بنَ مروانَ لم يَدَعْ ... من المالِ إلاَّ مُسْحَتاً أو مُجَلَّفُ
(And the bite of a time, O son of Marwān, that has left of wealth nothing but what is wiped out or stripped bare.)
The reading of the rest is from the three-letter سَحَتَه, which is the dialect of the Ḥijāz. The basic sense of this root is exhaustiveness and depletion; from it is "the barber sahata the hair", i.e. took it all and left none of it; and it is used for destroying and doing away with. Its accusative is by an implied «أَنْ» in answer to the prohibition. When al-Zamakhsharī cited al-Farazdaq's saying «إلاَّ مُسْحَتاً أو مُجْلَّفُ», he said after it: "in a verse over the settling of whose parsing knees have not ceased knocking together."
I say: he means that this verse is difficult to parse. Since he has mentioned it, let me mention the transmissions of this verse and what people have said about it, as befits this place. So I say, and with Allah is the power: this verse is transmitted in three versions, none of which is free of poetic licence (ḍarūra). The first: «لم يَدَعْ» with a fatḥa on the yāʾ and the dāl, and «مُسْحَت» in the accusative. In this there are five views.
First: the meaning of "it has left of wealth nothing but what is wiped out" is "nothing remained but what is wiped out"; so since this is equivalent to a fāʿil (agent), he conjoined to it his saying «أو مُجَلَّفُ» in the nominative. al-Zamakhsharī adduced this verse as evidence for the reading of Ubayy and al-Aʿmash «فَشربوا منه إلاَّ قليلٌ» with «قليل» in the nominative, and that has already been treated. Second: it is nominative by an implied verb indicated by «لم يَدَعْ», the implied form being: "or there remained what is stripped". Third: «مُجَلَّفُ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is implied, its implied form being: "or what is stripped is likewise"; this is the explanation of al-Farrāʾ. Fourth: it is conjoined to the latent pronoun in «مُسْحتاً»; properly, there should have been a separation between them by a tawkīd (emphasis) or some separator, but the one who holds this, namely al-Kisāʾī, does not stipulate it; moreover, it is permitted in poetic licence according to all. Fifth: «مُجَلَّف» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) on the measure of the passive participle, like His saying: {كُلَّ مُمَزَّقٍ} [Sabaʾ: 19], i.e. "stripping" and "tearing apart"; on this view it is conjoined to «عَضُّ زمانٍ», since the implied form is: "the cares of hopes hurled us, and the bite of time, or stripping"; so it is a fāʿil by virtue of being conjoined to the fāʿil. This is the view of al-Fārisī, and to me it is the best of them.
The second version: a fatḥa on the yāʾ, a kasra on the dāl, and «مُسْحت» in the nominative. Its explanation is clear: it is from وَدَع في بيته يَدِع فهو وادع ("he stayed at rest in his house"), meaning "remained, remains, so it is remaining". So «مُسْحَتٌ» is nominative as fāʿil, and «مُجَلَّفُ» is nominative by conjunction with it. In that case there must be an omitted pronoun, its implied form being "on its account" or "because of it" . . . . the discussion.
The third version: «يُدَعْ» with a ḍamma on the yāʾ and a fatḥa on the dāl, as a passive, «مُسْحَت» nominative because it stands in place of the fāʿil, and «مُجَلَّف» conjoined to it. The wāw ought properly not to have been dropped, but kept, because it does not fall between a yāʾ and a kasra; it was dropped only by treating the passive like the active. There is longer discussion on the verse than this, which I have left out for brevity; this is its core. I have mentioned it in al-Baqara, explained its meaning and its vocabulary, and connected it to what precedes it; so do turn to it.

semin-durr:63-63.t:
His saying: {إِنْ هذان}: the readers differed on this noble verse. Ibn Kathīr alone read «إنْ هذانِّ» with a light «إنْ», the alif, and a doubled nūn. Ḥafṣ likewise, except that he made the nūn of «هذانٍ» light. Abū ʿAmr read «إنَّ» doubled and «هذين» with yāʾ and a light nūn. The rest likewise, except that they read «هذان» with alif.
As for the first reading, the reading of Ibn Kathīr and Ḥafṣ, it is the clearest of the readings in meaning, wording and script. That is because they made «إنْ» lightened from the heavy one, so it was made inoperative; and since it was made inoperative — the more eloquent of its two options — it was feared that it might be confused with the negative [إنْ], so the lām was brought into the khabar (predicate) as a distinguisher. So «هذان» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «لَساحران» its khabar; and it agrees with the script of the codex, for the spelling is «هذن», without alif or yāʾ, and the explanation of that will come.
As for the doubling of the nūn of «هذان», it is according to what was stated in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ, and I treated it thoroughly there.
As for the Kufans, they claim that «إنْ» is negative, meaning «ما», and the lām means «إلاَّ»; it is a well-known disagreement. Their explanation here agrees with someone's reading «ما هذانِ إلاَّ ساحران».
As for the reading of Abū ʿAmr, it is clear in terms of parsing and meaning. As for the parsing, «هذَيْن» is the noun of «إنَّ», the sign of its accusative being the yāʾ, and «لَساحِران» is its khabar, the lām having entered for emphasis. As for the meaning: they affirmed sorcery of the two in an emphatic way at both its ends. But they found it problematic with regard to the script of the codex, because its spelling is «هذن» without alif or yāʾ, so writing it with yāʾ is an addition to the script of the codex. Abū Isḥāq said: "I do not permit the reading of Abū ʿAmr, because it contradicts the codex." Abū ʿUbayd said: "I saw them in al-Imām, the codex of ʿUthmān, as «هذن», with no alif in it; and thus I saw the nominative of the dual in that codex with the alif dropped; and when they wrote the accusative and genitive they wrote it with yāʾ and did not drop it."
I say: Abū ʿAmr should not be refuted with this. How many things have come in the script that lie outside analogy, and they have stated explicitly that it is not permitted to read according to them; so let this be one of them, I mean of what lies outside analogy. If you say: what you transmitted from Abū ʿUbayd is a charge that applies equally to Abū ʿAmr and the others; for just as they objected to him for adding the yāʾ, they can be objected to for adding the alif, since the alif is present in their reading and absent from the script of the codex — the answer is what has already been said of Abū ʿUbayd's statement, that he saw them dropping the alif in the nominative of the dual, whereas when they wrote the accusative and genitive they wrote it with yāʾ.
A group, among them ʿĀʾisha (may Allah be pleased with her) and Abū ʿAmr, held that this is one of the places where the scribe made a mistake, and it was recited correctly.
They mean that he ought to have written it with yāʾ but did not, and people read it only with yāʾ, correctly.
As for the reading of the rest, there are several views on it. First: «إنَّ» means «نَعَمْ» ("yes"), «هذان» is a mubtadaʾ and «لَساحران» its khabar. «إنَّ» frequently occurs in the meaning of «نعم», and they cited:
3297 - بَكَرَ العَواذِلُ في المَشِيْ ... بِ يَلُمْنَني وأَلوْمُهُنَّهْ
ويَقلْن شَيْبٌ قد عَلا ... كَ وقد كَبِرْتَ فقلتُ إنَّهْ
(The censuring women came early about my grey hair, blaming me while I blamed them; they say: "Grey hair has come over you, and you have grown old"; and I said: "Yes [innah].")
i.e. "and I said: yes", the hāʾ being the hāʾ of pause (hāʾ al-sakt). A man said to Ibn al-Zubayr: "May Allah curse a she-camel that carried me to you!" He said: «إنَّ وصاحبَها», i.e. "yes, and [may He curse] its rider". This is the view of al-Mubarrad and ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān among others. It is rejected on two grounds. First: «إنَّ» meaning «نعم» is not established, and what he cited is to be interpreted otherwise: as for the verse, the hāʾ is its noun and the khabar is omitted because the meaning is understood, its implied form being "it is so". As for Ibn al-Zubayr's saying, that is by omission of what is conjoined to and keeping the conjoined (maʿṭūf), and omission of the khabar of «إنَّ» because there is indication of it, its implied form being "it and its rider are cursed"; and there is an evident strain in this. Second: the entry of the lām on the khabar of a mubtadaʾ not emphasised by «إنَّ» with kasra; for such a thing occurs only in poetic licence, as in [the poet's] saying:
3298 - أمُّ الحُلَيْسِ لَعَجُوْزٌ شَهْرَبَهْ ... تَرْضَى من اللحمِ بعظمِ الرَّقَبَهْ
(Umm al-Ḥulays is indeed a decrepit old woman, content, of meat, with the bone of the neck.)
It may be answered: «لَساحِران» may be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ on which this lām has entered, its implied form being "they two are sorcerers" (lahumā sāḥirān). al-Zajjāj did that, as will come in the report from him.
Second: its noun is the pronoun of the story (ḍamīr al-qiṣṣa), which is the «ها» before «ذان», and it is not the «ها» of drawing attention that enters on demonstratives; the implied form is: "the story is: these two are sorcerers". They rejected this on two grounds. First: on the ground of the script: had it been so, it should have been written «إنها», attaching the pronoun to the particle before it, as in His saying: {فَإِنَّهَا لاَ تَعْمَى الأبصار} [al-Ḥajj: 46]; their writing it separate from «إنَّ» and joined to the demonstrative prevents its being a pronoun, and this is clear. Second: it leads to the lām of the beginning (lām al-ibtidāʾ) entering on a khabar not affected by an abrogating governor. It may be answered with what has been said above.
Third: its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), omitted, and the clause made up of the mubtadaʾ and khabar after it is in the position of nominative as the khabar of «إنَّ»; the implied form is: "it, i.e. the matter and the affair, [is that]...". This was weakened on two grounds. First: the omission of the noun of «إن», which is not permitted except in poetry, on condition that «إنَّ» is not directly followed by a verb, as in [the poet's] saying:
3299 - إنَّ مَنْ يَدْخُلِ الكنيسةَ يوماً ... يَلْقَ فيها جَآذراً وظِباءَ
(Whoever enters the church one day will find in it young wild calves and gazelles.)
Second: the entry of the lām on the khabar.
al-Zajjāj answered that it enters on an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "they two are sorcerers". His teacher al-Mubarrad approved of this, I mean his answer by that.
Fourth: «هذان» is its noun and «لَساحران» its khabar. This was rejected on the ground that it ought to be «هذين» with yāʾ, as in the reading of Abū ʿAmr.
It was answered that it is according to the dialect of Banū al-Ḥārith, Banū [Translator's note: the source has «وبين», for «وبني».] al-Hujaym, Banū al-ʿAnbar, Zubayd, ʿUdhra, Murād and Khathʿam. The great authorities reported this dialect, such as Abū al-Khaṭṭāb, Abū Zayd al-Anṣārī and al-Kisāʾī. Abū Zayd said: "I heard among the Arabs some who change every yāʾ preceded by a fatḥa into alif." They make the dual like the maqṣūr (noun ending in short alif), keeping an alif in all its cases and making its inflection implied (muqaddar) with the vowels. They cited [the poet's] saying:
3300 - فأَطْرَق إطْراقَ الشُّجاعِ ولو يرى ... مَسَاغاً لِناباه الشُّجاعُ لصَمَّما
(He lowered his head as the serpent lowers its head; and had the serpent seen a way in for its two fangs, it would have bitten deep.)
i.e. «لنابَيْه»; and his saying:
3301 - إنَّ أباها وأبا أباها ... قد بَلَغا في المجدِ غايتاها
(Her father and her father's father have reached, in glory, its two utmost ends.)
i.e. «غايتيهما», among other pieces of evidence.
Ibn Masʿūd read: «أنْ هذان ساحِران» with a fatḥa on «أَنْ» and the lām dropped, on [the view] that it and what is within its scope are a badal (substitute) of «النجوى»; al-Zamakhsharī said so, and al-Shaykh followed him and did not object to it. It is open to question, because the interposition of the clause of saying between the badal and what it substitutes for is not valid. Moreover, the clause of saying is explicative of «النجوى» in the reading of the generality, and al-Zamakhsharī himself said so at first; so how can «أنْ هذان ساحران» validly be made a badal of «النجوى»?

His saying: {بِطَرِيقَتِكُمُ}: the bāʾ in «بطريقتكم» makes [the verb] transitive, like the hamza. The meaning is: "with the people of your way". It has also been said: «الطريقة» is an expression for the chiefs, so there is no omission.

semin-durr:64-64.t:
His saying: {فَأَجْمِعُواْ}: Abū ʿAmr read «فاجْمَعُوا» with a connecting alif (hamzat al-waṣl) and a fatḥa on the mīm; the rest with a disjunctive [hamza] with fatḥa and a kasra on the mīm. The verification of that has already been given in Sūrat Yūnus, together with what people said about the difference between the three-letter and the four-letter [verb].
«كيدَكم» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). It has also been said: it is by removal of the preposition, i.e. "upon your plot"; and that is nothing.

His saying: {صَفّاً}: it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «ائتُوا», i.e. "come lined up", i.e. "in a row", so it is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun). It has also been said: it is a mafʿūl bihi, i.e. "come [to] a people in a row", with naming by the maṣdar in it; or it is by omission of the muḍāf, i.e. "people of a row".

His saying: {وَقَدْ أَفْلَحَ}: al-Zamakhsharī said: "A parenthesis (iʿtirāḍ), meaning: and whoever prevails has won." I say: by the parenthesis he means that this clause was brought in as something foreign between their speech and what they said; because part of their saying is «قالوا يا موسى: إمَّا أَنْ تُلْقي», and this clause, I mean His saying «وقد أفلَح», is from the speech of Allah the Exalted, so it is a parenthesis in this respect.
