It is open to question, because the apparent sense is that it is part of what they said: they said it to urge their people to fight; and in that case there is no parenthesis.

semin-durr:65-65.t: His saying: {إِمَّآ أَن تُلْقِيَ}: there are several views on it. First: it is accusative by an implied verb, its implied form being "choose one of the two matters"; so al-Zamakhsharī implied it. al-Shaykh said: "This is an explanation of meaning, not an explanation of parsing; the explanation of parsing is: 'either you choose the casting'." Second: it is nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being: "the matter is either your casting or our casting"; so al-Zamakhsharī implied it. Third: it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being: "your casting is first"; His saying «وإمَّا أَنْ نكونَ أولَ مَنْ أَلْقى» indicates it. al-Shaykh chose this and said: "So the correspondence is good in terms of meaning, even if correspondence in terms of the verbal construction is not obtained." Then he said: "In al-Zamakhsharī's implied form 'the matter is your casting' there is no correspondence." The like of this was treated earlier in al-Aʿrāf.

semin-durr:66-66.t:
His saying: {فَإِذَا حِبَالُهُمْ}: this fāʾ is a conjunction joining [it] to an omitted clause indicated by the context; the implied form is: "so they cast, and lo...". This «إذا» is the one of surprise (al-mufājaʾa). There are three views on it, given previously. First: it keeps its status as an adverb of time. Second: it is an adverb of place. Third: it is a particle.
al-Zamakhsharī said: "The precise account of it is that it is the one with the meaning of time, which requires a governor to put it in the accusative and a clause to which it is annexed; it has been specialised in some places in that its governor is a specific verb, namely the verb of surprising, and the clause is nominal only. So the implied form of His saying {فَإِذَا حِبَالُهُمْ وَعِصِيُّهُمْ} is: 'Mūsā was surprised by the time of the imagined running of their ropes and their staffs'; [this is a representation, and the meaning is: upon their ropes and their staffs surprising him, making running appear to him." End of quotation.]
al-Shaykh said: "His saying that it is temporal is the weaker view, and it is the doctrine of al-Riyāshī. His saying 'which requires a governor' is correct. His saying 'and a clause to which it is annexed' is not correct according to some of our colleagues, because it is either the khabar (predicate) of a mubtadaʾ (subject) or governed by the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; and if that is so, it is impossible for it to be annexed to the clause, because it is either part of the clause or governed by part of it, so annexation is impossible. His saying 'it has been specialised in some places ...' to the end — we have already explained its governor. His saying 'and the clause after it is nominal only' — this restriction is not correct; rather al-Akhfash allowed, and stated explicitly, that a verbal clause joined with «قد» may occur after it, as in «خرجْتُ فإذا زيدٌ قد ضربه عمروٌ» ('I went out, and lo, Zayd — ʿAmr had struck him'), with «زيد» in the nominative, or in the accusative by al-ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb). His saying 'and the meaning is: upon their ropes and their staffs surprising him, making running appear to him' — this is the reverse of what he implied; rather the meaning is: upon their ropes and their staffs surprising him. If you said: «خَرَجْتُ فإذا السَّبُعُ» ('I went out, and lo, the beast of prey'), the meaning is: the beast surprised me and its appearance came upon me suddenly." End of what he rejected [him] with.
His statement [Translator's note: i.e. al-Shaykh's.] and what he rejected him with are not binding on him [al-Zamakhsharī], because he refutes him with the view of some grammarians, and he [al-Zamakhsharī] does not commit himself to that view so that he could be refuted with it, especially when the well-known view is otherwise; and his aim is an explanation of meaning.
Abū al-Baqāʾ said: the fāʾ is the answer to what was omitted, its implied form being "so they cast, and lo"; so «إذا» in this is an adverb of place, its governor being «أَلْقَوْا». This is open to question, because this implied «أَلْقَوْا» does not require an answer such that he could say "the fāʾ is its answer"; rather he ought to have said: the fāʾ conjoins this clause of surprise to another implied clause. His saying "an adverb of place" is the doctrine of al-Mubarrad, and also the apparent view of Sībawayh, though the well-known view is that it remains temporal. His saying "its governor is «فأَلْقَوا»" is not permissible, because the fāʾ prevents that.
This is the statement of al-Shaykh; then he said after it: "And because this «إذا» is only governed by the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, which is «حبالُهم وعِصِيُّهم», unless he makes it itself stand in the position of the khabar; because the khabar may be «يُخَيَّل», and «إذا» and «يُخَيَّل» may be in the position of ḥāl (circumstantial)."
This is parallel to «خرجْتُ فإذا الأسدُ رابضٌ» and «رابضاً» ("I went out, and lo, the lion crouching"). If you put «رابض» in the nominative, «إذا» is governed by it, the implied form being "at hand the lion is crouching", or "in the place". If you put it in the accusative, «إذا» is the khabar. For that reason it and the nominative after it suffice as a complete sentence, as in: «خَرَجْتُ فإذا الأسدُ» ("I went out, and lo, the lion").

His saying: {يُخَيَّلُ إِلَيْهِ}: the generality read «يُخَيَّل» with a ḍamma on the first yāʾ and a fatḥa on the second, as a passive; and «أنَّها تَسْعى» is nominative by the verb before it, because it stands in place of the fāʿil (agent), its implied form being "their running was made to appear to him". Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed two other views on it. First: what stands in place of the fāʿil is the pronoun of the ropes and staffs; it was made masculine, and He did not say «تُخَيَّل» with the upper-dotted tāʾ, because the femininity of the ropes is not real. Second: what stands in place of the fāʿil is a pronoun referring to what was cast, and for that reason it was made masculine. On both views there are two views on His saying «أنها تسعى». First: it is a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) of that latent pronoun in «يُخَيَّل». Second: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the latent pronoun as well; the meaning is: "it was made to appear to him as possessing running". There is no need for this; moreover, they have stated explicitly that an interpreted maṣdar does not occur in the position of a ḥāl: if you said «جاء زيدٌ أَنْ يركضَ», meaning "running", in the sense of "possessing running", it would not be permissible.
Ibn Dhakwān read «تُخَيَّلُ» with the upper-dotted tāʾ. There are three views on it. First: the verb is attributed to the pronoun of the ropes and staffs, i.e. "the ropes and staffs were made to appear", and «أنَّها تَسْعَى» is a badal ishtimāl of that pronoun. Second: likewise, except that «أنَّها تَسْعى» is a ḥāl, i.e. "possessing running", as established above. Third: the verb is attributed to His saying «أنَّها تَسْعى», like the reading of the generality in one of its views; the verb was made feminine only because the nominative acquires femininity through annexation, since the implied form is "their running (saʿyuhā) was made to appear to him"; so it is like [the poet's] saying:
3302 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . شَرِقَتْ صدرُ القناةِ من الدمِ
(... the head of the spear was choked with blood.)
[and His saying:] {فَلَهُ عَشْرُ أَمْثَالِهَا} [al-Anʿām: 160].
Abū al-Sammāl read «تَخَيَّلُ» with a fatḥa on the tāʾ and the yāʾ, as active; the original is «تَتَخَيَّلُ», one of the two tāʾs having been dropped, as in: {تَنَزَّلُ الملائكة} [al-Qadr: 4]; and «أنَّها تسعى» is again a badal ishtimāl of that pronoun. Ibn ʿAṭiyya also allowed it to be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). Ibn Jubāra al-Hudhalī transmitted the reading of Abū al-Sammāl as «تُخَيِّل» with a ḍamma on the upper-dotted tāʾ and a kasra on the yāʾ; so the verb is attributed to the pronoun of the ropes, and «أنها تسعى» is an object, i.e. "the ropes made their running appear". Ibn ʿAṭiyya attributed this reading to al-Ḥasan and ʿĪsā al-Thaqafī.
Abū Ḥaywa read «نُخَيِّل» with the nūn of majesty, and «أنها تسعى» is again a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) in this reading.
al-Ḥasan and al-Thaqafī read «عُصِيُّهم» with a ḍamma on the ʿayn wherever it occurs, and that is the original. The ʿayn was given a kasra only in harmony with the ṣād, and the ṣād was given a kasra in harmony with the yāʾ. The original is ʿuṣuww with two wāws; it was modified, as you see, by changing the two wāws into two yāʾs because they are heavy, then the ṣād was given a kasra so that [the yāʾ] would be sound, and the ʿayn was given a kasra in harmony. The author of «al-Lawāmiḥ» transmitted that the reading of al-Ḥasan is «عُصْيهُم» with a ḍamma on the ʿayn, a sukūn on the ṣād and a light yāʾ, with the nominative; it is also a plural like [the reading of] the generality, except that it is on the pattern fuʿl, like ḥumr, while the first is on the pattern fuʿūl, like fulūs.
The clause «يُخَيَّل» may be in the position of nominative as the khabar of «هي» [Translator's note: so in the source; the mubtadaʾ in the verse is «حبالُهم وعِصِيُّهم».], on [the view] that the «إذا» of surprise is a complement (faḍla); or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, on [the view] that the «إذا» of surprise is the khabar. The pronoun in «إليه» most apparently refers to Mūsā. It has also been said: it refers to Pharaoh. His saying {فَأَوْجَسَ فِي نَفْسِهِ خِيفَةً موسى} indicates the first.

semin-durr:69-69.t:
His saying: {تَلْقَفْ}: the generality read it with a fatḥa on the lām, a doubled qāf and the fāʾ jussive (majzūm), as the answer to the command. It has already been stated that Ḥafṣ reads «تَلْقَفْ» with a sukūn on the lām and a light qāf. Ibn Dhakwān read here «تَلْقَفُ» in the nominative, either as a ḥāl (circumstantial) or as resumptive. The verb «تَلْقَف» was made feminine by treating it according to the meaning of «ما», because its meaning is the staff; had it been made masculine, going by its wording, that would have been permissible, but it was not read so.
[Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The fāʿil (agent) of «تَلْقَف» may be the pronoun of Mūsā"; on this view «تلقفُ» in the nominative reading may be a ḥāl from «موسى». There is remoteness in that.]

His saying: {كَيْدُ سَاحِرٍ}: the generality [read] «كَيْدُ» in the nominative, as the khabar (predicate) of «إنَّ», «ما» being a relative noun and «صَنَعُوا» its ṣila (relative clause), with the returning pronoun omitted; the relative is the noun [of «إنَّ»], and the implied form is: "what they have made is the plot of a sorcerer". «ما» may also be maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya), so there is no need for a returning pronoun, and the parsing remains as it is; the implied form is: "their making is the plot of a sorcerer".
Mujāhid, Ḥumayd and Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «كَيْدَ» in the accusative, as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), «ما» being redundant and preparatory (muhayyiʾa).
The two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read «كيدُ سِحْر», on [the view] that the meaning is "the plot of people of sorcery"; or they were made sorcery itself, for intensification; or [it is] a specification of the plot, because a plot may be sorcery or not sorcery, just as all numbers are specified by what explains them, as in "a hundred dirhams" and "a thousand dinars"; and like it: "the science of jurisprudence", "the science of grammar". Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«كيدُ ساحر» is annexation of the maṣdar (verbal noun) to its agent, and «كيدُ سِحْر» is annexation of the genus to the species."
The rest [read] «ساحر». He made «ساحراً» singular even though a group is meant by it. al-Zamakhsharī said: "Because the aim in this speech is the sense of genus, not the sense of number; had it been put in the plural, it would have been imagined that number is what is intended."

semin-durr:71-71.t:
His saying: {فَلأُقَطِّعَنَّ}: the like of this has already been treated. «مِنْ خِلافٍ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "on opposite sides". «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the extent; the precise account of this, and what was read there, has also been given previously.

His saying: {فِي جُذُوعِ النخل}: it may be literal; in the exegesis [it is said] that he hollowed out palm trunks until he made them hollow, put them inside, and they died of hunger and thirst. Or it may be figurative, and that has two aspects. First: one particle has been put in place of another, the original being "upon the palm trunks", as in the saying of the other [poet]:
3303 - بَطَلٌ كأنَّ ثيابَه في سَرْحَةٍ ... يحذى نِعالَ السَّبْتِ ليس بتوءَمِ
(A hero — as though his clothes were upon a tall tree — shod with sandals of tanned leather, not one of twins.)
Second: their being firmly fixed was likened to the firm fixing of one whom the trunk encloses and contains. An instance of «صَلَب» (to crucify) being made transitive with «في» is [the poet's] saying:
3304 - وقد صَلَبُوا العَبْدِيَّ في جِذْعِ نَخْلَةٍ ... فلا عَطَسَتْ شَيْبانُ إلاَّ بأَجْدَعا
(They crucified the ʿAbdī on the trunk of a palm tree; so may Shaybān never sneeze except with a cut-off nose.)

His saying: {أَيُّنَآ أَشَدُّ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). This clause takes the place of the two objects if «عَلِمَ» has its proper sense [of knowing that], and the place of one if it is [the ʿalima] of acquaintance (ʿirfāniyya). On making it of acquaintance, «أيُّنا» may be a relative noun meaning «الذي», made indeclinable because it is annexed and the head of its ṣila (relative clause) has been omitted; «أشَدُّ» is then the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, the clause made of that mubtadaʾ and this khabar is the ṣila of «أيّ», and «أيّ» with what is within its scope is in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), like His saying: {ثُمَّ لَنَنزِعَنَّ مِن كُلِّ شِيعَةٍ أَيُّهُمْ أَشَدُّ عَلَى الرحمن} [Maryam: 69] in one of its views, as stated previously.

semin-durr:72-72.t:
His saying: {والذي فَطَرَنَا}: there are two views on it. First: the wāw is a conjunction, conjoining this relative noun to «ما جاءنا», i.e. "we will never prefer you over what has come to us, nor over the One who created us". They put mention of the Creator, exalted is He, last only because it belongs to the category of ascending from the lower to the higher. Second: it is the wāw of oath, the relative noun being what is sworn by, and the answer to the oath is omitted, i.e. "by the right of the One who created us, we will not prefer you over the truth". The answer may not be «لن نُؤْثرك», according to those who allow placing the answer first, because an oath is not answered with «لن» except in anomalous speech.

His saying: {مَآ أَنتَ قَاضٍ}: two views are possible on «ما». The more apparent: it is a relative noun meaning «الذي», «أنت قاضٍ» being its ṣila (relative clause), and the returning pronoun omitted, i.e. «قاضِيه»; its omission is permitted, even though it is in the genitive, because its position is accusative; i.e. "so decree what you are decreeing". Second: it is maṣdar-forming and temporal (maṣdariyya ẓarfiyya); the implied form is: "so decree your affair for as long as you are decreeing". Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned that. Some forbade that, I mean making it maṣdar-forming, saying: because maṣdar-forming «ما» is not given a nominal clause as its ṣila. This prohibition is not agreed upon; rather a large group allowed it. Ibn Mālik reported that this is frequent when «ما» indicates time, and cited:
3305 - واصِلْ خليلَك ما التواصُلُ مُمْكِنٌ ... فَلأَنْتَ أَوْ هُوَ عن قليلٍ ذاهِبُ
(Keep in touch with your friend as long as keeping in touch is possible, for you or he will soon be gone.)
and that it is rare when it is not temporal, and cited:
3306 - أحْلامُكُمْ لِسَقَامِ الجَهْلِ شافيةٌ ... كما دِماؤُكُمُ تَشْفي مِن الكَلَبِ
(Your forbearance cures the sickness of ignorance, as your blood cures rabies.)

His saying: {إِنَّمَا تَقْضِي هذه الحياة}: two views are possible on this «ما». First: it is the preparatory [ما] (al-muhayyiʾa) allowing «إنَّ» to enter on the verb, and «الحياةَ الدنيا» is an adverb of «تَقضي», whose object is omitted, i.e. "you decree your aim and your affair". «الحياةَ» may also be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) by extension of usage (ittisāʿ); the reading of Abū Ḥaywa «تقضى هذه الحياةُ», with the verb passive and «الحياة» nominative as standing in place of the fāʿil (agent), indicates that; for usage was extended with it, so it stood in place of the fāʿil and was made nominative.
Second: «ما» is maṣdar-forming and is the noun of «إنَّ», the khabar (predicate) being the adverb; the implied form is: "your decreeing is in this worldly life", meaning: you have this world only, and we have the Hereafter.
Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "If it was read in the nominative, it is the khabar of «إنَّ»." He means: had «الحياة» been read in the nominative, it would be the khabar of «إنَّ», and its noun would then be «ما», a relative noun meaning «الذي», whose returning pronoun is omitted, its implied form being: "what you decree is this life, not anything else".

semin-durr:73-73.t:
His saying: {وَمَآ أَكْرَهْتَنَا}: two views are possible on this «ما». First: it is a relative noun meaning «الذي». On its position there are two possibilities. First: it is in the position of accusative, by conjunction with «خطايانا», i.e. "that He may forgive us also that which you compelled us to". The second of the two possibilities: it is in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), the khabar (predicate) being omitted, its implied form being: "and that sorcery to which you compelled us is removed from us", or "we will not be taken to account for it", and the like.
The second view: it is negative. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "There is a fronting in the speech, its implied form being: 'that He may forgive us our sins of sorcery, and you did not compel us to it'." This is far from the meaning; the apparent view is the first.
«من السحرِ» may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in «عليه» or from the relative noun; it may also be for explaining the genus.

semin-durr:74-74.t: His saying: {إِنَّهُ مَن يَأْتِ}: the hāʾ is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and the conditional clause is its khabar (predicate). «مُجْرِماً» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «يأْتِ». His saying {لاَ يَمُوتُ} may be a ḥāl from the hāʾ in «له», or a ḥāl from «جهنَّم», because the clause contains a pronoun of each of them.

semin-durr:76-76.t: [His saying: {جَنَّاتُ}: a badal (substitute) of «الدرجات», or an explicative (bayān).] Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The implied form may not be 'they are gardens', because «خالدين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and on this implied form there would be nothing in the speech to govern the second; whereas on the first, the governor of the ḥāl is the being-settled (al-istiqrār) or the meaning of pointing."

semin-durr:77-77.t:
His saying: {طَرِيقاً}: there are two views on it. First: it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), by way of figurative speech: the road results from striking the sea, since the meaning is "strike the sea so that it splits for them and becomes a road"; by this the attribution of striking to the road is valid. It has also been said: «ضرب» here means «جَعَلَ», i.e. "make for them a road and open it in it". Second: it is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf). Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The implied form is 'the place of a road', so it is a mafʿūl bihi on the apparent level; its parallel is His saying {أَنِ اضرب بِّعَصَاكَ البحر} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 63], and it is like 'I struck Zayd'. It has also been said: «ضرب» here means «جعل» and «شرع», like their saying 'I assigned him a share (ḍarabtu lahu bi-sahm)'." End of quotation. His saying "on the apparent level" means that were it not for the interpretation it would be an adverb.

His saying: {يَبَساً}: an adjective of «طريقاً». It was described with it on account of what it would become, because it was not yet dry; only the east wind passed over it and dried it, as is reported in the exegesis. Is it originally a maṣdar (verbal noun) used as a description for intensification, or by omission of a muḍāf, or the plural of yābis, like khādim and khadam, with which the singular is described for intensification, as in [the poet's] saying:
3307 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ومِعَىً جِياعاً
(... and a hungry gut.)
i.e. like a hungry company, it being described thus because of the excess of its hunger?
al-Ḥasan read «يَبْساً» with a sukūn; it is also a maṣdar. It has also been said: the one with fatḥa is a noun and the one with sukūn a maṣdar. Abū Ḥaywa read «يابساً», an active participle.

His saying: {لاَّ تَخَافُ}: the generality [read] «لا تَخاف» in the nominative, and there are several views on it. First: it is resumptive, so it has no grammatical position. Second: it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «اضرِبْ», i.e. "strike, not fearing". Third: it is an adjective of «طريقاً», the returning pronoun being omitted, i.e. "in which you do not fear".
Ḥamza alone among the Seven [read] «لا تَخَفْ» in the jussive (majzūm), as a prohibition. There are several views on it. First: it is a resumptive prohibition. Second: it is likewise a prohibition, in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the fāʿil of «اضرِبْ», or as an adjective of «طريقاً», as stated for the reading of the generality, except that this requires implying a [verb of] saying, i.e. "it being said to you", or "a road about which it is said: do not fear"; as in [the poet's] saying:
3308 - جاؤوا بمَذْقٍ هل رَأَيْتَ الذئبَ قَطّ
(They brought diluted milk [of a colour as if to say:] "Have you ever seen the wolf?")
Third: it is jussive as the answer to the command, i.e. "if you strike a dry road, you will not fear".

His saying: {وَلاَ تخشى}: it was read only with the alif retained. Someone said that whoever read «لا تَخَفْ» in the jussive should properly have read «لا تَخْشَ» with it dropped; that is nothing, because recitation is a followed practice (sunna). There are several views on it. First: it is a ḥāl. There is a difficulty in that: the imperfect negated with «لا» is like the affirmative in that the wāw is not directly prefixed to it. Its interpretation is by omission of a mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "while you do not fear", as in [the poet's] saying:
3309 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... نَجَوْتُ وأَرْهَنُهم مالِكا
(... I escaped, leaving Mālik with them as a pledge.)
Second: it is resumptive: the Exalted informed him that no fear would befall him.
Third: it is jussive by the implied (muqaddar) dropping of the vowel, as in [the poet's] saying:
3310 - إذا العَجوْزُ غَضِبَتْ فَطَلِّقِ ... ولا تَرَضَّاها ولا تَمَلَّقِ
(If the old woman gets angry, divorce her; do not try to please her and do not flatter.)
and the saying of the other:
3311 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... كَأَنْ لم تَرَى قبلي أسيراً يمانيا
(... as though you had never seen a Yemeni captive before me.)
and from it is {فَلاَ تنسى} [al-Aʿlā: 6] on one of the two views, treating the weak letter like a sound letter. A good number of such cases was given to you in Sūrat Yūsuf at {مَن يَتَّقِ} [verse: 90]. Fourth: it is likewise jussive, by dropping of the weak letter, and this alif is not that one, I mean the final radical of the word; it is only an alif of prolongation (ishbāʿ), brought in to agree with the verse-ends and the heads of the verses; so it is like the alif in His saying: {الرسولا} [al-Aḥzāb: 66], {السبيلا} [al-Aḥzāb: 67] and {الظنونا} [al-Aḥzāb: 10]. These views are needed only on the reading of «لا تَخَفْ» in the jussive; as for whoever read it in the nominative, this is conjoined to it.
Abū Ḥaywa read «دَرْكاً» with a sukūn on the rāʾ. al-darak and al-dark are [two nouns] from al-idrāk (overtaking), i.e. "Pharaoh and his troops will not overtake you". The discussion of them has already been given in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ, [where it was stated] that the Kufans read it with sukūn, as Abū Ḥaywa does here.

semin-durr:78-78.t:
His saying: {بِجُنُودِهِ}: there are several views on it. First: the bāʾ is for the ḥāl (circumstantial); that is on [the view] that «أَتْبَعَ» is transitive to two [objects], the second of which has been omitted; the implied form is: "so Pharaoh made his punishment follow them". al-Shaykh implied it as "his chiefs and his retinue"; the first is better. Second: the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) on the second object; the implied form is: "so Pharaoh made his troops follow them"; so it is like His saying: {وَلاَ تُلْقُواْ بِأَيْدِيكُمْ} [al-Baqara: 195] [and the poet's saying]:
3312 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . لا يَقْرَأْن بالسُّوَرِ
(... they do not recite the sūras.)
«أتبع» has indeed come as transitive to two [objects], both explicit; He said: «وَأَتْبَعْنَاهُم. . . .». Third: it makes [the verb] transitive, on [the view] that «أَتْبَعَ» may be transitive to one [object] in the sense of "with"; on this view the bāʾ may also be for the ḥāl — indeed that is the more apparent.
Abū ʿAmr in one transmission and al-Ḥasan read «فاتَّبَعَهُمْ» with doubling; and so is al-Ḥasan's reading throughout the Quran, except in His saying: {فَأَتْبَعَهُ شِهَابٌ ثَاقِبٌ} [al-Ṣāffāt: 10].

His saying: {مَا غَشِيَهُمْ}: [it is] the fāʿil (agent) of «غَشِيَهم». This belongs to concision and to the comprehensive expressions (jawāmiʿ al-kalim) whose wording is little and whose meaning is much, i.e. "there covered them what none knows the true nature of except Allah the Exalted". al-Aʿmash read «فَغَشَّاهم» with doubling. On the fāʿil in that case there are three views. First: it is «ما غَشَّاهم», as in the preceding reading, i.e. "there covered them of the sea what covered them".
Second: it is the pronoun of the Creator, exalted is He, i.e. "so Allah covered them". Third: it is the pronoun of Pharaoh, because he was the cause of their destruction. On these two views, «ما غَشَّاهم» is in the position of accusative as the second object.

semin-durr:80-80.t:
His saying: {قَدْ أَنجَيْنَاكُمْ}: The two brothers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) read «قد أَنْجَيْتُكم», «واعَدْتُكم» and {رَزَقْتُكم} with the tāʾ of the first-person speaker singular; the rest read «أَنْجَيْناكم», «رَزَقْناكم» and «واعَدْناكم» with the nūn of majesty. They agreed on «ونَزَّلْنا». The difference of Abū ʿAmr over «وَعَدْنا» was discussed earlier, in al-Baqara. Ḥumayd read «نَجَّيْناكم» with shadda.
«الأَيْمَنِ» has also been read in the genitive. al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is a genitive by adjacency (jiwār), as in their saying «جُحْرُ ضَبٍّ خَرِبٍ» ('a hole of a lizard, ruined')." But the Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) declared it irregular and weak, and analysed it as an adjective (naʿt) of «الطُّور», saying: "It is so described because of the blessing (yumn) in it, or because it lies on the right of one who faces the mountain."
{جانبَ} is a second object (mafʿūl) with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "the approach to the side of". It is not permissible for the second object to be omitted. {جانب} is an adverbial (ẓarf) of the promise, and the implied meaning is: "We promised you the Torah in this place", because it is a specific adverb of place, to which the verb does not reach by itself. If it were said that latitude is allowed with this adverb, so that it is made a direct object (mafʿūl bihi), i.e. made the very thing promised, like «سِيْر عليه فرسخان وبريدان» ('two farsakhs and two post-stages were travelled on it'), that would be permissible.

semin-durr:81-81.t:
His saying: {فَيَحِلُّ}: The majority read «فيحِلُّ» with kasra on the ḥāʾ and on the lām of «يَحْلِلْ». al-Kisāʾī, with others, read both with ḍamma. Ibn ʿUtayba agreed with the majority on the ḥāʾ and with al-Kisāʾī on the lām. The reading of the majority is from «حَلَّ عليه كذا», i.e. "it became due" (wajaba), from «حَلَّ الدَّيْنُ يَحِلُّ», i.e. its payment became due. Of this is His saying: {حتى يَبْلُغَ الهدي مَحِلَّهُ} [al-Baqara: 196], and also {وَيَحِلُّ عَلَيْهِ عَذَابٌ مُّقِيمٌ} [al-Zumar: 40]. The reading of al-Kisāʾī is from «حَلَّ يَحُلُّ», i.e. "to alight", and of this is {أَوْ تَحُلُّ قَرِيباً مِّن دَارِهِمْ} [al-Raʿd: 31].
The well-known view is that the agent (fāʿil) of «يَحلُّ» in both readings is «غضبي». The author of «al-Lawāmiḥ» said: "It is a direct object (mafʿūl bihi), and the agent was left out because it is well known; the implied meaning is: 'your transgression would bring down upon you My anger', and «ولا تَطْغَوا» points to it. It is not permissible to attribute it to «غضبي» so that it would be nominative as its agent." Then he said: "The object may be omitted when there is evidence for it, namely «العذاب» and the like." I say: in his view «حَلَّ» is transitive by itself, because it is from «الإحلال», as he stated explicitly. And when it is from «الإحلال» it takes one object, and that object is either «غضبي», the agent then being a pronoun referring back to the transgression, as he implied it, or it is omitted and the agent is «غضبي». There is awkwardness in his wording.
Ṭalḥa read «لا يَحِلَّنَّ عليكم» with the prohibitive «لا», kasra on the ḥāʾ, fatḥa on the lām of «يَحِلَّنَّ» and the doubled nūn of emphasis, i.e. "do not expose yourselves to transgression so that My anger becomes due upon you"; it belongs to the type «لا أُرَيَنَّك ههنا» ('let me not see you here').
Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «ولا تَطْغُوا» with ḍamma on the ghayn, from «طغا يَطْغُو», like «غدا يَغْدو».
As for His saying {فَيَحِلَّ}: it may be jussive (majzūm), conjoined to «لا تَطْغَوا»; so said Abū l-Baqāʾ, but there is room for objection in it, since the meaning is not a prohibition of anger's descending upon them. The second possibility is that it is accusative through an implied «أَنْ» in the response; and that is clear.

semin-durr:83-83.t: His saying: {وَمَآ أَعْجَلَكَ}: mubtadaʾ and khabar; «ما» is interrogative, asking the reason for going ahead of his people. al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: «ما أَعْجلك» is a question about the reason for the haste, so the fitting answer would be to say: 'seeking more of Your pleasure, longing for Your speech and the fulfilment of Your promise'; yet His saying {هُمْ أولاء على أَثَرِي} is, as you see, not fitting to it. I say: what the Lord of Might addressed him with contained two things. One: denial of the haste itself. The second: a question about the cause of the thing denied and what moved him to it. The more important of the two matters to Moses was to spread out his excuse and prepare the ground for the cause in the very thing that was denied him. So he pleaded that nothing had occurred from him except a slight advance, the like of which is not counted in custom nor made much of, and that between him and those he had gone ahead of there was only a short distance, by the like of which the head of a delegation and its vanguard go ahead of them. Then he followed it with the answer to the question about the cause, saying: {وَعَجِلْتُ إِلَيْكَ رَبِّ لترضى}."

semin-durr:84-84.t:
His saying: {هُمْ أولاء على أَثَرِي}: like His saying {ثُمَّ أَنْتُمْ هؤلاء تَقْتُلُونَ} [al-Baqara: 85]. «على أَثَري» may be a second khabar, or a ḥāl (circumstantial).
The majority read «اُوْلاء» with a hamza with kasra. al-Ḥasan and Ibn Muʿādh read it with a yāʾ with kasra, replacing the hamza with yāʾ for ease. Ibn Wathāb read «أُوْلاَ» shortened, without hamza. A group read «أولايَ» with yāʾ with fatḥa, which is close to a mistake.
The majority read «أَثَري» with fatḥa on the hamza and on the yāʾ. Abū ʿAmr, in the transmission of ʿAbd al-Wārith, and Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «إثْري» with kasra on the hamza and sukūn on the yāʾ. ʿĪsā read it with ḍamma and sukūn on the yāʾ, and al-Kisāʾī reported it as a dialect.

semin-durr:85-85.t: His saying: {وَأَضَلَّهُمُ}: The general run of readers take it as a past verb attributed to al-Sāmirī. Abū Muʿādh, with others, read «وأَضَلُّهم» nominative as a mubtadaʾ, being an elative (afʿal al-tafḍīl, comparative-superlative); and «السامريُّ» is its khabar.

semin-durr:86-86.t:
His saying: {غَضْبَانَ أَسِفاً}: two ḥāls. The detailed treatment of this has already been given in Sūrat al-Aʿrāf.
His saying: {وَعْداً حَسَناً}: it may be a confirmatory maṣdar (verbal noun), with the second object omitted, its implied form being "He promises you the Book and guidance", or the second object may be left out so as to be general. It may also be that «الوعد» has the meaning of "that which is promised", in which case it is itself the second object.
His saying: {مَّوْعِدِي}: a maṣdar. It may be annexed to its agent, meaning: "Did you find that I broke what I promised you?"; or it may be annexed to its object, meaning that they had promised him to hold fast to his religion and his party.

semin-durr:87-87.t:
His saying: {بِمَلْكِنَا}: The two brothers read it with ḍamma on the mīm; Nāfiʿ and ʿĀṣim with fatḥa; the rest with kasra. It has been said that these are dialects of one meaning, like «النَّقْض» and «النِّقْض», and that the meaning is power and dominion. But al-Fārisī and others distinguished between them, saying: "The ḍamma means: 'We had no dominion that we might break Your promise by its authority; rather we did it by consideration and personal judgement'; so the meaning is that they had no dominion."
As in the saying of Dhū l-Rumma: 3313 - «لا تُشْتكى سَقْطَةٌ منها وقد رَقَصَتْ ... بها المفاوِزُ حتى ظهرُها حَدِبُ» (No stumble of hers is complained of, though the deserts made her dance until her back was humped), i.e. no stumble occurs from her so that it would be complained of. The fatḥa of the mīm is a maṣdar of «مَلَكَ أمرَه»; the meaning: "We did not do it by being masters of the right course; rather our souls overcame us." The kasra of the mīm is frequent for what the hand takes and holds, but it is used for matters that a person settles; its meaning is like that of the preceding one. In these two cases the maṣdar is annexed to its agent and the object is omitted, i.e. "by our mastery of the right course".
His saying: {حُمِّلْنَآ}: Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥafṣ read it with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ and a doubled mīm with kasra. Abū Jaʿfar read likewise except that he lightened the mīm; the rest read both with fatḥa and a light mīm. In the first and second readings they attributed the act to others, and in the third they attributed it to themselves.
{أَوْزَاراً} is a second object in all but the third reading. {مِّن زِينَةِ} may be attached to «حُمِّلْنا», or attached to an omitted element as an adjective (ṣifa) of «أَوْزار».
His saying: {فَكَذَلِكَ}: an adjective of a maṣdar, or, according to Sībawayh, a ḥāl of its pronoun, i.e. "a casting like our casting, al-Sāmirī cast".

semin-durr:89-89.t:
His saying: {أَلاَّ يَرْجِعُ}: The majority read «يرجعُ» (nominative) because «أن» is the lightened form of the heavy «أنَّ». What shows this is the occurrence of its full form, the doubled one, in His saying: {أَلَمْ يَرَوْاْ أَنَّهُ لاَ يُكَلِّمُهُمْ} [al-Aʿrāf: 148].
Abū Ḥaywa, al-Shāfiʿī and Abān read it accusative, making it the subjunctive-governing «أنْ». The "seeing" in the first case is certain knowledge, and in the second it is sight. These two views were discussed in detail in Sūrat al-Māʾida.
«السامريُّ» is attributed to a tribe called Sāmira.
al-Aʿmash read «فنسْي» with sukūn on the sīn, which is a eloquent dialect. The pronoun in «نسي» may refer to al-Sāmirī, in which case it is the speech of Allah the Exalted; or it may refer to Moses, peace be upon him, in which case it is the speech of al-Sāmirī, i.e. "he forgot his god". Both views are transmitted from the exegetes.

semin-durr:90-90.t: The majority read «إنما فُتِنْتُم» and «إنَّ ربَّكم الرحمنُ» with kasra in both, because they come after speech (qawl) and do not mean supposition. A group read both with fatḥa, and this was explained by the dialect of Sulaym, who put fatḥa on «أنَّ» after «القول» in every case. Abū ʿAmr in one transmission, and al-Ḥasan and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar, read «أنَّ ربَّكم» only with fatḥa. This was explained in two ways. One: that it and what follows it are in the sense of a maṣdar in the position of nominative, as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "and the matter is that your Lord is al-Raḥmān", so this is a conjoining of sentences, not a conjoining of single words. The second: that it is genitive through an implied preposition, i.e. "because your Lord is al-Raḥmān, so follow me". The like of this, in relation to this «فاء», has been discussed earlier.

semin-durr:92-92.t: And «إذْ» is accusative by «مَنَعَك», i.e. "What prevented you at the time of their going astray?"

semin-durr:93-93.t: There are two views about «لا» in it. One: that it is redundant (mazīda), i.e. "what prevented you from following me". The second: that it entered by being carried over to the meaning, since the meaning is: "What moved you not to follow me, and what called you to follow me?". ʿAlī ibn ʿĪsā mentioned it. The detailed treatment of these two views has already been given, praise be to Allah, at the beginning of al-Aʿrāf.

semin-durr:94-94.t:
The discussion and reading of «يا بنَ أُمَّ» has already been given.
The majority read the lām of «اللِّحْيةِ» with kasra, which is the most eloquent. Fatḥa is also found in it, and ʿĪsā ibn Sulaymān al-Ḥijāzī read it so; fatḥa is the dialect of the Ḥijāz. Its plural is «لِحَى», like «قِرَب». Ḍamma has also been reported for it, as they said «صِوَر» with kasra, though its due is ḍamma. The bāʾ in «بلِحْيَتي» is not redundant: either because the meaning is "let no seizing come from you", or because the object is omitted, i.e. "do not seize me". Whoever claimed it is redundant, like the one in {وَلاَ تُلْقُواْ بِأَيْدِيكُمْ} [al-Baqara: 195], has been far-fetched.
His saying: {وَلَمْ تَرْقُبْ قَوْلِي}: this sentence is in the position of accusative, as a conjunction (nasaq) [upon] {فَرَّقْتَ بَيْنَ بني إِسْرَآئِيلَ}, i.e. "that you should say: 'You divided them', and that you should say: 'You did not heed my word'", i.e. did not . . . [Translator's note: the source text breaks off here with an ellipsis.]
Abū Jaʿfar read «تُرْقِبْ» with ḍamma on the imperfect prefix, from «أَرْقَبَ».

semin-durr:95-95.t: His saying: {فَمَا خَطْبُكَ}: mubtadaʾ and khabar. «الخَطْب» has been discussed in Yūsuf. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said here: "It implies a rebuke, as if he said: 'What is your ill omen and your misfortune?'" The Shaykh rebutted him with the saying of the Exalted: {قَالَ فَمَا خَطْبُكُمْ أَيُّهَا المرسلون} [al-Ḥijr: 57].

semin-durr:96-96.t:
His saying: {بَصُرْتُ}: It is said «بَصُرَ بالشيءِ», i.e. he knew it, and «أبصرَه», i.e. he looked at it. So said al-Zajjāj. Others said: "«بَصُرَ به» and «أبصره» both mean 'he knew'."
The majority read the ṣād with ḍamma in the past and in its imperfect. al-Aʿmash and Abū l-Sammāl read «بَصِرْتُ» with kasra and «يَبْصَروا» with fatḥa, which is a dialect. ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd read both verbs in the passive, i.e. "I was informed of what they were not informed of."
The two brothers read «تَبْصُروا» (second person), addressing Moses and his people, or in veneration of him, like His saying {إِذَا طَلَّقْتُمُ النسآء} [al-Ṭalāq: 1] and the saying: 3314 - «. . . . . . . حَرَّمْتُ النساءَ سواكُمُ ... . . . . . . .» (I have forbidden women other than you . . .). The rest read in the third person, about his people.
The majority read «قَبْضَة» with fatḥa on the qāf; it is the single instance of «قَبَضَ». al-Zamakhsharī said: "As for «القَبْضَة», it is the single act of seizing, and applying it to the thing seized is naming the object by the maṣdar." I say: the grammarians say that a maṣdar so used does not take the feminine tāʾ; you say «هذه حُلَّةٌ نَسْجُ اليمن» ('this is a robe, the weave of Yemen') and not «نَسْجَةُ اليمن». They object with this verse, then answer that what is forbidden is only the tāʾ indicating singularity (taḥdīd), not mere feminine marking; and this tāʾ indicates mere feminine marking. Likewise His saying {والأرض جَمِيعاً قَبْضَتُهُ} [al-Zumar: 67].
al-Ḥasan read «قُبْضَة» with ḍamma on the qāf, like «الغُرْفَة» and «المُضْغَة», in the sense of "what is scooped" and "what is seized". From him «قُبْصَة» with unpointed ṣād was also reported. «القَبْض» with the pointed ḍād is with the whole palm, and with the unpointed ṣād it is with the tips of the fingers. It has parallels, such as «الخَضْم», eating with the whole mouth, and «القَضْم», with the front of it; «القَصْم» is breaking with separation, and «الفَصْم» with fāʾ is breaking with continuity. Something of this was discussed in al-Baqara.
Ibn Muḥayṣin assimilated the pointed ḍād into the tāʾ of the first-person speaker while keeping the emphatic quality (iṭbāq), as discussed earlier [under] «بَسَطْتَ». The two brothers and Abū ʿAmr assimilated the dhāl into the tāʾ in «فَنَبَذْتُها».

semin-durr:97-97.t:
His saying: {لاَ مِسَاسَ}: The majority read it with kasra on the mīm and fatḥa on the sīn. It is a maṣdar of «فاعَل», like «القِتال» from «قاتَل», so it requires mutual participation. In the exegesis: "Do not touch me, and I shall not touch you", and whoever touched him was struck by fever.
al-Ḥasan, Abū Ḥaywa, Ibn Abī ʿAbla and Qaʿnab read it with fatḥa on the mīm and kasra on the sīn. I say: so the Shaykh expressed it, following Abū l-Baqāʾ. If we took this wording at face value it would have to be read «مَسِيس», with the alif turned into yāʾ because of the kasra before it; but that was not reported, so they must have meant by "kasra" the imāla. What shows what I say is what al-Zamakhsharī said: "«لا مَساسِ» has also been read, on the pattern of «فَجارِ». Like it is their saying about the gazelles: 'If they come to the water, then no ʿabāb, and if they miss it, then no abāb'; these are proper names (aʿlām) for the single touch, the single drink and the single seeking («الأَبَّة» being the single act of «الأَبّ», seeking)." This is his explicit statement that the alif remains as it was.
Likewise the saying of the author of «al-Lawāmiḥ» shows it: "It is in the form of «نَزَالِ» and «نَظارِ», of the verb-nouns (asmāʾ al-afʿāl) meaning 'get down' and 'look'", which is also an explicit statement that the alif stays as it was. Then the author of «al-Lawāmiḥ» said: "These nouns of this pattern are definite, and the negative «لا» that makes indefinite nouns accusative, as in «لا مالَ لك», does not enter them; rather, in it is a negation of the act, so its implied meaning is: 'there shall be no touching from you', and its meaning is prohibition, i.e. 'do not touch me'."
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«لا مَساسِ» is a deviation from the maṣdar, like «فَجارِ» and the like. Abū ʿUbayda and others compared it to «نزالِ» and «دَراكِ» and the like, and the comparison is right in that they are all deviations; but it differs in that those deviate from the imperative, while «مَساس» and «فَجار» deviate from the maṣdar. Of this is the saying of the poet: 3315 - «تميمٌ كرَهْطِ السَّامِرِيِّ وقَوْلِه ... ألا لا يريدُ السَّامِرِيُّ مَساسِ» (Tamīm are like the clan of al-Sāmirī and his saying: 'Hear! al-Sāmirī wants no touching')."
The words of al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya give that «مَساس» in this reading deviates from the maṣdar, like «فَجار» from «الفَجَرة»; whereas the words of the author of «al-Lawāmiḥ» require that it deviates from an imperative verb, unless he meant that it is a deviation in the way a verb-noun is a deviation, as Ibn ʿAṭiyya explained the words of Abū ʿUbayda earlier.
His saying: {لَّن تُخْلَفَهُ}: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read it with kasra on the lām, in the active. The rest read it with fatḥa, in the passive. Abū Nahīk, as Ibn Khālawayh reports from him, read it with fatḥa on the upper tāʾ and ḍamma on the lām; the author of «al-Lawāmiḥ» reports likewise from him, except with the lower yāʾ. Ibn Masʿūd and al-Ḥasan read it with ḍamma on the nūn of majesty and kasra on the lām.
As for the first reading, its meaning is: "you will never find it broken", like your saying «أَحْمَدْتُه» and «أَجْبَنْتُه», i.e. I found him praiseworthy and cowardly. It is also said that the meaning is: "it will reach you, and you will not be able to dodge or swerve from it." al-Zamakhsharī said: "This is from «أَخْلَفْتُ الوعدَ» when you find it broken. al-Aʿshā said: 3316 - «أثوى وقَصَّر لَيْلَةً لِيُزَوَّدا ... فمضى وأَخْلَفَ مِنْ قُتَيْلَةَ مَوْعِدا» (He stayed, and cut short a night to be provisioned, then he went on, and found Qutayla's appointment broken)."
The meaning of the second: "Allah will not break His promise which He promised you." As for the two readings of Abū Nahīk, they are from «خَلَفَه يَخْلُفُه» when it comes after him, i.e. the appointed time that is yours will not repel your word that you say. It is a problematic reading. Abū Ḥātim said: "We do not know any basis for the reading of Abū Nahīk." As for the reading of Ibn Masʿūd, the verb in it is attributed to Allah the Exalted, and the first object is omitted, i.e. "He will not break it for you."
His saying: {ظَلْتَ}: The majority read it with fatḥa on the ẓāʾ followed by a lām with sukūn. Ibn Masʿūd, Qatāda, al-Aʿmash (with a difference reported from him), Abū Ḥaywa, Ibn Abī ʿAbla and Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar [read it] with kasra on the ẓāʾ. From Ibn Yaʿmar ḍamma was also reported. Ubayy and al-Aʿmash in the other transmission read «ظَلِلْتَ» with two lāms, the first with kasra.
As for the reading of the majority, in it one of the two like letters is dropped, and the ẓāʾ is kept with its own vowel; it was dropped only for lightness. Sībawayh counted it among the irregular (shādhdh), meaning irregular in analogy, not in usage, and he counted other words with it, such as «مَسْتُ» and «أَحَسْتُ», as in the verse: 3317 - «. . . . . . . أَحَسْنَ به فهنَّ إليه شُوْسُ» (they sensed him, and they are looking sideways at him). Ibn al-Anbārī counted «هَمْتُ» for «هَمَمْتُ». This dropping occurs only when the lām of the verb has sukūn. Some later scholars mentioned that this dropping is analogical in every verb whose ʿayn and lām are doubled and whose lām has sukūn, and that is in the dialect of Sulaym.
What I say is: whenever the doubling mentioned meets a kasra, as in «ظَلِلْتُ» and «مَسِسْتُ», the dropping is analogical. Does ḍamma take the place of kasra in this? The apparent answer is that it does, indeed all the more, because ḍamma is heavier than kasra, as in «غُضْنَ يا نسوةُ», i.e. «أغْضُضْنَ أبصارَكُنَّ» ("lower your gazes, women"); Jamāl al-Dīn Ibn Mālik mentioned it. As for fatḥa, the dropping in it is weak, as in «قَرْن يا نسوةُ في المنزل» ('stay, women, in the house'), and of this, in one of the two explanations of the reading of {وَقَرْنَ فِي بُيُوتِكُنَّ} [al-Aḥzāb: 33], as will come, God willing.
As for the kasra, its explanation is that he moved the kasra of the lām to the fāʾ (first radical) after stripping that of its own vowel, to point to it. As for the ḍamma, it may be that a dialect exists on the pattern «فَعَل يفعُل» with fatḥa on the ʿayn in the past and ḍamma in the imperfect, and then it was moved as explained for the kasra. As for «ظَلِلْت» with two lāms, this is the original, and it alerts to the others. And {عاكفاً} is the khabar of «ظَلَّ».
His saying: {لَّنُحَرِّقَنَّهُ}: the response to an omitted oath, i.e. "By Allah, we shall surely burn it". The majority read it with ḍamma on the nūn and kasra on the doubled rāʾ, from «حَرَّقه يُحرِّقُه» with intensification. There are two interpretations of it. The clearer is that it is from «حَرَّقه بالنار» (burned it with fire). The second: that it is from «حَرَق نابُ البعير», when one of the camel's tusks gnashes against another; the sound heard from it is called «الصَّريف». The meaning: "we shall file it down with a file, a filing by which we destroy it, as the camel does with its tusks, one on another."
al-Ḥasan, Qatāda and Abū Jaʿfar read «لَنُحْرِقَنَّه» with ḍamma on the nūn, sukūn on the ḥāʾ and kasra on the rāʾ, from «أحرق» (four-letter verb). Ibn ʿAbbās, Ḥumayd, ʿĪsā and Abū Jaʿfar read «لَنَحْرُقَنَّه» likewise except that he gave the rāʾ ḍamma. It may be that «أَحْرق» and «حرَّق» have one meaning, like «أَنْزل» and «نزَّل». As for the last reading, it means "we shall file it down with a file".
His saying: {لَنَنسِفَنَّهُ}: The majority read fatḥa on the first nūn, sukūn on the second, and a light kasra on the sīn. ʿĪsā read the sīn with ḍamma. Ibn Miqsam read the first nūn with ḍamma, the second with fatḥa, and the sīn with kasra and shadda. «النَّسْف» is scattering and winnowing; it is also said: uprooting something from its base. It is said «نَسَفَه يَنْسِفُه» with kasra on the sīn, and with ḍamma, in the imperfect, and on this rest the two readings. The shadda is for intensification.

semin-durr:98-98.t:
His saying: {وَسِعَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ عِلْماً}: The majority read the sīn with kasra, light. In this reading «عِلْماً» is a tamyīz (specification) transferred from the agent, since the original is «وَسِعَ عِلْمُه كلَّ شيءٍ». Mujāhid and Qatāda read the sīn with fatḥa and shadda. In the accusative of «علماً» in that case [there are two views]. One: that it is a direct object. al-Zamakhsharī said: "Its explanation is that «وَسِع» is transitive to one object, and «عِلْماً» is accusative as tamyīz, being the agent in meaning. When it was intensified, it was transferred to transitivity with two objects, so both are put in the accusative as objects, because the specifier is an agent in meaning, just as you say of «خاف زيد عمراً»: «خَوَّفْت زيداً عمراً»; thus by the transfer you return what was an agent to being an object." Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "The meaning is: He gave everything knowledge", so he made it include the sense of «أعطى». What al-Zamakhsharī said is preferable.
The second view: that it is also a tamyīz, as in the light reading. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "There is also another possibility: that it means 'He magnified the creation of everything', such as the earth and the heaven, and that is in the sense of «بَسَط» (spread out), so «علماً» would be a tamyīz." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "He widened the creation of things and multiplied them by origination."

semin-durr:99-99.t: His saying: {كذلك نَقُصُّ}: The kāf is either an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, or a ḥāl of the pronoun of that implied maṣdar. The implied form: "We relate, like Our relating of this strange report." «من أنباءِ» is an adjective of an omitted element which is the object of «نَقُصُّ», i.e. "We relate a report from among the reports of".

semin-durr:100-100.t: His saying: {مَّنْ أَعْرَضَ}: «مَنْ» may be conditional or relative. The conditional sentence, or the predicative sentence resembling it, is in the position of accusative as an adjective of «ذِكْراً».

semin-durr:101-101.t:
His saying: {خَالِدِينَ}: a ḥāl of the agent of «يَحْمِلُ». If it is asked: how can a plural occur as a ḥāl of a singular? The answer is that it was carried over onto the wording of «مَنْ», so the pronoun is singular in «أَعْرَضَ», «فإنَّه» and «يَحْمِلُ», and onto its meaning, so it is plural in «خالدين» and «لهم». The pronoun in «فيه» refers to «وِزْراً». What is meant is the punishment caused by the burden, which is the sin, so the cause is put in the place of the caused.
Dāwūd ibn Rufayʿ read «يُحَمَّلُ» with doubling, in the passive, and what stands in place of the agent is the pronoun of «مَنْ»; «وِزْراً» is a second object.
His saying: {وَسَآءَ}: this is the «ساء» that means «بِئْس». Its agent is latent in it, referring to «حِمْلاً», accusative as tamyīz, because in this chapter the pronoun is explained by what follows it. The implied form: «وساء الحِمْل حِمْلاً». The specific object of blame is omitted, its implied form being: «وساء الحِمْل حِمْلاً وِزْرُهم». It is not permissible for the agent of «بِئْس» to be the pronoun of «الوِزْر», because the condition of the pronoun in this chapter is that it refer to the tamyīz itself. If you say: why do you reject that «ساء» contains the pronoun of «الوِزْر»? I say: it is not valid that «ساء», whose rule is that of «بِئْس», contain the pronoun of a specific, non-vague thing. Nor is it permissible that «ساء» here mean «أهمَّ» and «أحزنَ» (distressed, grieved), so as to be conjugated like other verbs. al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is enough to turn you away from it that the speech of Allah the Exalted would come to [your saying]: 'and the burden grieved them on the Day of Resurrection as a load', after you extricate yourself from the burden of this lām and of this accusative." End of quotation.
The lām in «لهم» is attached to an omitted element by way of clarification, like the one in {هَيْتَ لَكَ} [Yūsuf: 23].

semin-durr:102-102.t:
His saying: {يَوْمَ يُنفَخُ}: «يومَ» is a badal of «يومَ القيامة», or an explication of it, or it is accusative by an implied verb, or the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ. It is built on fatḥa according to the Kufans, like the reading of {هذا يَوْمَ يَنفَعُ} [al-Māʾida: 119], which has been discussed.
Abū ʿAmr read «نَنْفُخُ», active, with the nūn of majesty; the act is attributed to the one who commands it, out of veneration for the one commanded, who is the angel Isrāfīl. The rest read it with a yāʾ with ḍamma and fatḥa on the fāʾ, in the passive, and what stands in place of the agent is the preposition and its genitive noun after it. The majority read the wāw with sukūn. al-Ḥasan and Ibn ʿĀmir in one transmission read it with fatḥa, as the plural of «صُوْرَة», like «غُرَف» plural of «غُرْفَة». «الصور» was discussed in al-Anʿām.
«يَنْفُخُ» and «يَحْشُر» have also been read with a yāʾ with fatḥa, in the active, the agent being Allah the Exalted or the angel. al-Ḥasan, Ṭalḥa and Ḥumayd read «يُنْفَخ» like the majority, and «يَحْشر» with a yāʾ with fatḥa, in the active; the agent, as before, is the pronoun of the Creator or of the angel. It was also reported from al-Ḥasan «ويُحْشَر», in the passive, with «المجرمون» nominative by it. «زُرْقاً» is a ḥāl of «المجرمين»; what is meant is blueness of the eyes. The ḥāl came here with a quality resembling the inseparable, though its basis is non-inseparability; had you said in speech «جاءني زيدٌ أزرقَ العينِ» it would not be permissible except by interpretation.

semin-durr:103-103.t:
His saying: {يَتَخَافَتُونَ}: it may be resumptive (mustaʾnaf), or a second ḥāl of «المجرمين», or a ḥāl of the latent pronoun in «زرقاً», in which case it is a nested ḥāl, being a ḥāl from a ḥāl. The meaning of «يتخافتون» is: they speak secretly among themselves.
His saying {إِن لَّبِثْتُمْ إِلاَّ} is the object of the secret speaking. His saying {إِلاَّ عَشْراً}: nights may be meant, in which case dropping the tāʾ from the number is analogical; or days may be meant, in which case it is asked: why was the tāʾ dropped? It was said: if the counted noun is not mentioned in the number for the masculine, the tāʾ and its absence are both permissible. It is heard in their speech «صُمْنا من الشهر خمساً» ('we fasted five of the month'), though what is fasted is only the days, not the nights. In the ḥadīth: «مَنْ صامَ رمضانَ وأتبعه بسِتٍّ من شوال» ('whoever fasted Ramadan and followed it with six of Shawwāl'). The dropping is good here because it is the end of a verse and a pause.

semin-durr:104-104.t: His saying: {إِذْ يَقُولُ}: accusative by «أعلمُ», and «طريقةً» is accusative as tamyīz. [Translator's note: the source text reads «وطريقةً "نصبٌ» with a stray quotation mark, apparently a garbled reference to {أَمْثَلُهُمْ طَرِيقَةً}; translated as written.]

semin-durr:106-106.t:
His saying: {فَيَذَرُهَا}: there are two views about this pronoun. One: that it is the pronoun of «الأرض», implied because it is indicated. The second: the pronoun of «الجبال», on the basis of an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "He leaves their bases and settled places". «نَذَرُ» may mean "He leaves it empty", in which case «قاعاً» is a ḥāl; or it may mean the "making" sense of «يترك», in which case it takes two objects and «قاعاً» is the second.
About «القاع» there are statements. It is said: it is a pool of standing water, and its meaning does not suit here. The second: that it is the uncovered part of the earth; so said Makkī. The third: that it is the level place, and of this is the saying of Ḍirār ibn al-Khaṭṭāb: 3318 - «لَتَكُوْنَنَّ بالبطاحِ قُرَيْشٌ ... فَقْعَةَ القاع في أَكُفِّ الإِماءِ» (Quraysh in the valley-beds will be like a desert truffle of the plain in the hands of slave girls). The fourth: that it is land in which there is no plant and no building.
«الصَّفْصَف» is smooth land; it is also said: level land, so the two are close to synonyms. The plural of «القاع» is «أقْوع», «أَقْواع» and «قِيْعان».

semin-durr:107-107.t:
His saying: {لاَّ ترى فِيهَا عِوَجاً}: this sentence may be resumptive, or a ḥāl of «الجبال», or an adjective of the preceding ḥāl, which is «قاعاً» on one of the two interpretations, or an adjective of the second object on the other interpretation.
«العِوَج» has been discussed. al-Zamakhsharī said here: "If you say: they have distinguished between «العَوَج» and «العِوَج»; they said: «العِوَج» with kasra is for abstract things (maʿānī), and with fatḥa for concrete things (aʿyān), and the earth is a concrete thing, so how is kasra of the ʿayn valid in it? I say: the choice of this word has a fine and wonderful effect in describing the earth as level and smooth and negating crookedness from it in the most emphatic way. That is, if you took a piece of land and levelled it, and were thorough in levelling it by your eye and the eyes of the sighted, and you all agreed that no crookedness at all remained in it, and then you sought the opinion of the surveyor and ordered him to test its levelness by geometric measures, he would stumble on crookedness in more than one place, not perceived by the sense of sight but by geometric measure. So Allah the Exalted negated that crookedness which is too fine and subtle to be perceived, except by the measure known to the person of geometric calculation. And since that crookedness is not perceived except by measure and not by sensation, it was joined to abstract things, so «عِوج» was said of it with kasra."
«الأمْت» is slight protrusion. It is said: "He stretched his rope until there was no amt in it." It is also said: «الأمْت» is the mound, which is close to the first. It is also said: the cracks in the ground. It is also said: the hillocks.

semin-durr:108-108.t:
His saying: {يَوْمَئِذٍ}: accusative by «يَتَّبِعُون». It is also said: a badal of {يَوْمَ القيامة}; so said al-Zamakhsharī. There is room for objection in it because of the long separation. Also «يَتَّبِعُون» would remain unconnected with what precedes it, and the meaning would be lost by it. The implied form: "the day when the mountains are blown away".
His saying: {لاَ عِوَجَ لَهُ}: the sentence may be resumptive, or a ḥāl of «الداعي». The sentence may also be an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, its implied form being: "they follow him with a following that has no crookedness". Regarding the pronoun in «له» there are several views, the clearest being that it refers to «الداعي», i.e. there is no crookedness in his call, but he makes all of them hear, not inclining to some people over others. It is also said: it refers to that omitted maṣdar, i.e. no crookedness in that following. The third: that there is a reversal (qalb) in the speech, the implied form being «لا عِوَجَ لهم عنه» ('they have no turning away from him').
His saying: {إِلاَّ هَمْساً}: a direct object, and it is a "voided" exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh). «الهَمْس» is the faint sound. It is said: it is moving the lips without speech. al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is the faint murmur (rikz); from it are the voiceless letters (al-ḥurūf al-mahmūsa)." It is also said: it is what is heard of the fall of feet on the ground. From it «هَمَسَتِ الإبلُ», when that is heard from the fall of their hooves on the ground. He said: 3319 - «وهُنَّ يَمْشِيْنَ بنا هَمِيْسا ...» (and they walk with us at a hushed pace . . .).

semin-durr:109-109.t:
His saying: {يَوْمَئِذٍ}: a badal of what preceded, or accusative by what follows «لا», according to those who allow that. The implied form: "on the day when they follow, intercession will not benefit".
His saying: {إِلاَّ مَنْ أَذِنَ}: there are several views. One: that it is accusative as a direct object, and the governing word is «تَنْفَعُ»; «مَنْ» then refers to the one interceded for. The second: that it is in the position of nominative as a badal of «الشفاعة», and an omitted muḍāf is needed, implied as: "except the intercession of him for whom permission was given". The third: that it is accusative as an exception from «الشفاعة», with the omitted muḍāf implied, and on this it is a connected exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil). It may be a disconnected exception (munqaṭiʿ) if you imply nothing, and then it may be accusative, which is the dialect of the Ḥijāz, or nominative, which is the dialect of Tamīm. All these views are clear from what preceded, so I shall not lengthen with establishing them. «له» in the two places is for cause, like His saying {وَقَالَ الذين كَفَرُواْ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ} [al-Aḥqāf: 11], i.e. on account of him and on account of them.

semin-durr:111-111.t:
His saying: {وَعَنَتِ الوجوه}: It is said «عَنا يَعْنُو» when one is humbled and submits, and «أَعْناه غيرُه», i.e. someone else humbled him. From it comes «العُنَاة», plural of «عانٍ», which is the captive. He said: 3320 - «فيا رُبَّ مَكْروبٍ كرَرْتُ وراءَه ... وعانٍ فَكَكْتُ الغُلَّ عنه فَفَدَّاني» (How many a distressed one have I charged after, and how many a captive have I freed from his shackle, and he ransomed me). Umayya ibn Abī l-Ṣalt said: 3321 - «مَلِيكٌ على عَرْشِ السماء مُهَيْمِنٌ ... لِعِزَّته تَعْنُوا الوجوهُ وتَسْجُد» (A King on the throne of heaven, the Overseer; before His might faces submit and prostrate). In the ḥadīth: «فإنَّهنَّ عَوانٍ» ('for they are captives').
His saying: {وَقَدْ خَابَ}: this sentence may be resumptive, or a ḥāl, or parenthetical (iʿtirāḍ). al-Zamakhsharī said: "«وقد خابَ» and what follows is parenthetical, like your saying 'they failed and lost', for everyone who does wrong is a failure and a loser." By parenthesis here he means that he restricted «الوجوه» to the faces of the disobedient, so that the sentence entered between the disobedient and {وَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِنَ الصالحات}; this, in his view, is the counterpart of «وعَنَتِ الوجوهُ», and for this reason it is parenthetical. As for Ibn ʿAṭiyya, he made «الوجوه» general, and therefore made «وقد خابَ مَنْ حَمَل ظلماً» a balance for His saying {وَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِنَ الصالحات} to the end.

semin-durr:112-112.t:
His saying: {وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ}: a ḥāl sentence. His saying {فَلاَ يَخَافُ}: Ibn Kathīr read it jussive, as a prohibition. The rest read it nominative, as a negation and resumption, i.e. "so he does not fear".
«الهَضْم» is diminution. The Arabs say «هَضَمْتُ لزيدٍ مِنْ حقي», i.e. I reduced something of my right for Zayd; of it is «هَضِيم الكَشْحَيْن», i.e. slender in both flanks. Of it also is {طَلْعُهَا هَضِيمٌ} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 148], i.e. fine and packed, as though some of it wrongs another and so reduces its right. A man is «هضيم» and «مُهْتَضَم», i.e. wronged. «هَضَمْتُه», «اهْتَضَمْتُه» and «تَهَضَّمْتُه» all have one meaning. al-Mutawakkil al-Laythī said: 3322 - «إنَّ الأذِلَّةَ واللِّئامَ لَمَعْشَرٌ ... مَوْلاهُمُ المُتَهَضِّمُ المظلومُ» (The abject and the base are a company whose client is the oppressed, the wronged).
It is said that wrong (ẓulm) and diminution (haḍm) are close. Judge al-Māwardī distinguished between them, saying: "Ẓulm is withholding the whole of the right, and haḍm is withholding part of it."

semin-durr:113-113.t:
His saying: {وكذلك أَنزَلْنَاهُ}: a conjunction (nasaq) on {كذلك نَقُصُّ}. al-Zamakhsharī said: "And like that sending down; just as We sent down upon you these verses, We sent down the Qurʾān as a whole in this manner." Another said: "The meaning: just as We decreed these matters and made them truly lie in wait for the servants, so We warned these people about it and sent it down as a Qurʾān."
His saying: {مِنَ الوعيد}: an adjective of an omitted object, i.e. "We have set out in the Qurʾān a threat from among the threats", the genus being meant. «من» may be redundant according to the view of al-Akhfash regarding the direct object; the implied form: "We set out the threat in it".
al-Ḥasan read «أو يُحْدِثْ» like the group, except that he put sukūn on the lām of the verb. ʿAbd Allāh (Ibn Masʿūd), al-Ḥasan also in one transmission, Mujāhid and Abū Ḥaywa read «نُحْدِثْ» with nūn, also with sukūn on the lām. It was explained by treating the connected reading (waṣl) as the pause (waqf), or by putting sukūn on the verb as a dislike of the vowel, like the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays: 3323 - «فاليومَ أشرَبْ غيرَ مُسْتَحْقِبٍ ... . . .» (Today I drink, not laden with guilt . . .), and the saying of Jarīr: 3324 - «. . . . . . . . . ... أو نهرُ تيرى فلا تَعْرِفْكُمُ النَّفَرُ» (. . . or the river of Tīrā, so the tribe will not know you). Abū ʿAmr, as already said, did this with the rāʾ in particular, as in {يَنصُرُكُم} [Āl ʿImrān: 160].
«تُحْدِثُ» has also been read with the addressee's tāʾ, i.e. "you bring about".

semin-durr:114-114.t: His saying: {يقضى إِلَيْكَ وَحْيُهُ}: The majority read «يقضى» in the passive with «وَحْيُه» nominative as standing in place of the agent. al-Jaḥdarī, Abū Ḥaywa and al-Ḥasan, and it is the reading of ʿAbd Allāh (Ibn Masʿūd), read «نَقْضي» with the nūn of majesty in the active, «وَحْيَه» being a direct object. al-Aʿmash read likewise except that he put sukūn on the lām of the verb, disliking the vowel even though it is light on a weak letter. Instances of this have preceded in the reading of {مِنْ أَوْسَطِ مَا تُطْعِمُونَ أَهْلِيكُمْ} [al-Māʾida: 89].

semin-durr:115-115.t:
al-Yamānī read «فَنُسِي» with ḍamma on the nūn and shadda on the sīn, meaning: Satan made him forget.
His saying: {وَلَمْ نَجِدْ لَهُ عَزْماً}: «وجد» may be of knowing, so that it takes two objects, which are «له عَزْما»; or it may mean "to come upon", so that it takes one, which is «عَزْما». «له» is attached to the finding, or to an omitted element as a ḥāl of «عَزْما», since originally it is its adjective, put before it.

semin-durr:116-116.t: His saying: {أبى}: a resumptive sentence, because it is the answer to an implied question, i.e. "What prevented him from prostrating?", and it is answered that he refused and was arrogant. The object of refusal may be intended; in the other verse it is stated explicitly, in His saying {أبى أَن يَكُونَ مَعَ الساجدين} [al-Ḥijr: 31]. Omitting it here is made good by the verb being at the head of a verse-ending. It may also be that none is intended at all, and that the meaning is: "he is of the people of refusal and disobedience", without regard to what the refusal is attached to.

semin-durr:117-117.t: His saying: {فتشقى}: accusative by an implied «أَنْ» in the response to a prohibition. The prohibition is in form addressed to Iblīs, but the two of them (Adam and his wife) are meant, i.e. "do not engage in the causes of expulsion so that misery comes to you both", which is toil and worldly hardship in particular. It may be nominative as resumptive, i.e. "so you will be miserable"; so the Shaykh implied it. This is remote or impossible, since the aim is not to report that he will be miserable, but that if the expulsion of the two of them by Iblīs occurs, what was mentioned results. He attributed misery to him (Adam) and not to her because affairs are bound to the heads of men. What made that good was its being at the head of a verse-ending.

semin-durr:118-118.t: His saying: {إِنَّ لَكَ أَلاَّ تَجُوعَ}: in the position of accusative as the ism of «إنَّ»; the khabar is «لك». The implied form: "You have the absence of hunger and nakedness." So «تعرى» is accusative by implication, a conjunction on «تجوعَ». «العُرْي» is the skin's being stripped of something that protects it. It is said «عَرِي يعرى عُرِيَّاً». The poet said: 3325 - «وإنْ يَعْرَيْنَ إن كُسِيَ الجَواري ... فَتَنْبُو العينُ عن كَرَمٍ عِجافِ» (And if they go bare while the slave-girls are clothed, the eye turns away from noble, lean ones).

semin-durr:119-119.t:
His saying: {وَأَنَّكَ لاَ تَظْمَأُ}: Nāfiʿ and Abū Bakr read «وإنك» with kasra on the hamza; the rest read it with fatḥa. For one who read it with kasra, it may be resumptive, or a conjunction on the first «إنَّ». For one who read it with fatḥa, it is because he conjoined an interpreted maṣdar to the ism of the first «إنَّ». The khabar is the preceding «لك». The implied form: "You have the absence of hunger, the absence of nakedness, the absence of thirst and the absence of the midday sun." It is permissible for «أنَّ» with fatḥa to be the ism of «إنَّ» with kasra because of the separation between them; had it not been for that, it would not be permissible. If you said «إنَّ أنَّ زيداً قائم حَقٌّ» it would not be permissible, but when they are separated it is permissible. You say «إنَّ عندي أن زيداً قائم», where «عندي» is the khabar put before the ism, which is «أنَّ» and what is in its interpretation, because it is an adverbial; and the verse belongs to this type, the implied form being: «وإنَّ لك أنَّك لا تظمأ». al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: «إنَّ» does not enter «أنَّ», so one does not say «إنَّ أنَّ زيداً منطلق»; and the wāw stands in for «أنَّ» and takes its place, so why did it enter it? I say: the wāw was not set up to be always a substitute for «أنَّ»; it is a substitute for every governing element. Since it is not a particle set up for verification alone like «إنَّ», their combination is not barred, as the combination of «إنَّ» and «أنَّ» is barred."
«ضحى يَضْحَى» means to come out to the sun. ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa said: 3326 - «رَأَتْ رجلاً أَيْما إذا الشمسُ عارَضَتْ ... فيضحى وأيْما بالعَشِيِّ فَيَخْصَرُ» (She saw a man who, when the sun faces him, is exposed to it, and in the evening is chilled).
al-Zamakhsharī mentioned here a fine point in that the Exalted mentioned these things in negative wording without mentioning their opposites in affirmative wording, such as: "You have satiety, clothing, quenched thirst and shelter in the shade." He said: "He mentioned them in negative wording for their opposites, which are hunger, nakedness, thirst and exposure to the sun, so that the names of the kinds of misery of which He warned him would strike his ear, so that he would shun the cause that leads into them, out of aversion to them."

semin-durr:120-120.t: His saying: {فَوَسْوَسَ إِلَيْهِ}: «وَسْوَسَ إليه» means he conveyed the whispering to him. As for «وَسْوس له», its meaning is "for his sake". al-Zamakhsharī: "If you say: how is «وَسْوس» made transitive sometimes by lām, in His saying {فَوَسْوَسَ لَهُمَا الشيطان} [al-Aʿrāf: 20], and at other times by «إلى»? I say: Satan's whispering is like the wailing of the bereaved woman and the clucking of the hen, in that they are imitations of sounds, so their rule is that of a sound or a tinkle. From it is the whispering of one with delirium (al-mubarsam), and he is «مُوَسْوِس» with kasra; fatḥa is a mistake. Ibn al-Aʿrābī recited: 3327 - «وَسْوَسَ يَدْعو مُخْلِصاً رَبَّ الفَلَقْ» (He whispered, calling sincerely upon the Lord of the Daybreak). When you say «وَسْوَسَ له» its meaning is "for his sake", as in 3328 - «أجْرِسْ لها يا ابنَ أبي كِباشِ» (Make a sound for her, O son of Abū Kibāsh). The meaning of «وَسْوس إليه»: he conveyed the whispering to him, being in the sense of 'he mentioned to him'. And it may mean 'for his sake'."

semin-durr:121-121.t: His saying: {فغوى}: The majority read the wāw with fatḥa followed by an alif. Its explanation is clear. It is also said: its meaning is "he suffered indigestion" (bashima), from their saying «غَوِي البعير» with kasra on the wāw and the yāʾ, when that befalls it. Abū l-Baqāʾ reported this as a reading, and they explained it by this meaning. al-Zamakhsharī said: "From some of them: «فَغَوِيَ», meaning he suffered indigestion from eating much. Even if this is sound in the dialect of those who turn a yāʾ whose preceding letter has kasra into alif, saying of «فَنِي» and «بَقِي»: «فَنا» and «بَقا» (these are Banū Ṭayyiʾ), it is a vile explanation." I say: it seems he was not aware that it had been read with kasra on the wāw; had he been aware of it he would have rejected it. The one who says this has fled from ascribing error (ghayy) to Adam, peace be upon him.

semin-durr:124-124.t:
His saying: {ضَنكاً}: an adjective of «معيشة»; its origin is a maṣdar, and therefore it is not made feminine. It applies to singular, dual and plural with one wording.
The majority read «ضَنْكاً» with tanwīn in connected reading and its replacement by alif in pause, like all declinable words. A group read «ضنكى» with alif, like «سكرى». There are two possibilities for this alif. One: that it is a replacement for the tanwīn, with the connected reading treated as the pause, like parallels that have passed; the rest of them will come, God willing. The second: that it is the alif of feminine marking, the maṣdar being built on «فَعْلى» like «دعوى».
«الضَّنْك» is narrowness and hardship. It is said «ضَنُكَ عيشُه يَضْنُك ضَنَاكة وضَنْكاً». A woman is «ضِناك» when her body is fleshy, as though they imagined the narrowness of her skin by it.
The majority read «ونَحْشُرُه» with nūn and the verb nominative as resumptive. Abān ibn Taghlib, with others, put sukūn on the rāʾ. This allows two explanations. One: that the verb is jussive, conjoined to the position of the apodosis of the condition, which is the sentence {فَإِنَّ لَهُ مَعِيشَةً}, for its position is jussive; so it is like the reading of {مَن يُضْلِلِ الله فَلاَ هَادِيَ لَهُ وَيَذَرْهُمْ} [al-Aʿrāf: 186] with sukūn on the rāʾ. The second: that the sukūn is a sukūn of lightening, like {يَأْمُرْكُمْ} [al-Baqara: 67] and its like.
A group read it with the third-person yāʾ, the subject being Allah the Exalted or the angel. Abān ibn Taghlib in one transmission read «ونَحْشُرهْ» with sukūn on the hāʾ in connected reading. Its explanation is either by the dialect of Banū ʿUqayl and Banū Kilāb, or by treating the connected reading as the pause. «أعمى» is accusative as a ḥāl.

semin-durr:125-125.t: His saying: {وَقَدْ كُنتُ بَصِيراً}: a ḥāl sentence from the object of «حَشَرْتني». Nāfiʿ and Ibn Kathīr gave the yāʾ of «حَشَرْتني» fatḥa before the hamza.

semin-durr:126-126.t: His saying: {كذلك أَتَتْكَ}: Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "«كذلك» is in the position of accusative, i.e. 'a gathering like that', or 'We did the like of that', or 'a coming like that', or 'a recompense like your turning away', or 'forgetting'." In some of these views that he stated the kāf is accusative as a maṣdar, and in others accusative as a direct object. al-Zamakhsharī mentioned only the direct object, saying: "i.e. you did the like of that; then it is explained that Our signs came to you clear and luminous, yet you did not look at them with the eye of one who takes heed."

semin-durr:127-127.t: The Exalted's saying: {وكذلك نَجْزِي مَنْ أَسْرَفَ}: i.e. "and like that recompense We recompense him who transgressed".

semin-durr:128-128.t:
His saying: {أَفَلَمْ يَهْدِ لَهُمْ}: regarding the agent of «يَهْدِ» there are several views. One: that it is the pronoun of the Creator the Exalted. «يَهْدي» means "to make clear". The object of «يهدي» is omitted, its implied form being: "Has Allah not made clear to them the lessons and what He did to the denying nations?" Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "As to its agent there are two views, one of which is the pronoun of the name of Allah the Exalted, and he suspended «بَيَّن» here when it has the meaning of «اعلمْ», as He suspended it in His saying {وَتَبَيَّنَ لَكُمْ كَيْفَ فَعَلْنَا بِهِمْ} [Ibrāhīm: 45]." The Shaykh said: "«كم» here is informative (khabariyya), so the governing verb is not suspended from it." al-Zamakhsharī said: "It may contain the pronoun of Allah or of the Messenger, and the reading with nūn indicates this."
The second view: that the agent is a latent pronoun explained by what indicates it from the speech that follows. al-Ḥūfī said: "«كم أَهْلكنا» indicates the destruction of the generations. The implied form: 'Has the destruction of those We destroyed of the generations, and the effacing of their traces, not become clear to them, that they might take warning?'" Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "The agent is what is indicated by His saying {أَهْلَكْنَا}, i.e. 'Our destroying', and the sentence explains it."
The third view: that the agent is the following sentence itself. al-Zamakhsharī said: "The agent of «لم يَهْدِ» is the sentence after it, meaning: 'Has this not guided them, in its sense and content?' Its parallel is His saying {وَتَرَكْنَا عَلَيْهِ فِي الآخرين سَلاَمٌ على نُوحٍ فِي العالمين} [al-Ṣāffāt: 79], i.e. We left upon him this speech." The Shaykh said: "That a sentence is the agent of «يَهْدِ» is the Kufan school. As for his comparing and likening it to {وَتَرَكْنَا عَلَيْهِ فِي الآخرين سَلاَمٌ على نُوحٍ فِي العالمين}, «تركْنا» there has the sense of speech, so the sentence is quoted by it, as though it were said: 'We said upon him' and 'We applied to him this expression'; and a sentence is quoted by the sense of saying as it is quoted by saying."
The fourth view: that it is the pronoun of the Messenger ﷺ, because he is the one who makes clear to them, by what is revealed to him, the reports of past nations and bygone generations. This view was reported earlier from Abū l-Qāsim al-Zamakhsharī.
The fifth view: that the agent is omitted. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said, quoting others: "The agent is implied, its implied form being: guidance, or the matter, or looking and taking heed." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This, to my mind, is the best of the implications."
The Shaykh said: "It is the saying of al-Mubarrad, and it is not good, since it contains omission of the agent, which the Basrans do not permit; its improvement is to say: the agent is a latent pronoun, implied as 'yahdi huwa', i.e. the guidance." I say: this saying does not say the agent is omitted, but that it is implied («مقدر»), and the word «مقدر» is often used for the latent pronoun. As for the object of «يَهْدِ», there are two views: one, that it is omitted; the second, that it is the sentence of «كم» and what is within its scope, because it suspends it, so it fills the place of its object.
The sixth view: that the agent is «كم»; so said al-Ḥūfī, and he (al-Ḥūfī) rejected it in whoever said it, because «كم» is interrogative and what precedes it does not govern in it. The Shaykh said: "It is not interrogative here but informative." The Shaykh preferred that the agent be the pronoun referring to Allah the Exalted, saying: "The best of the explanations is that the agent be a pronoun referring to Allah the Exalted, as though He said: 'Has Allah not made clear?' The object of «يُبَيِّن» is omitted, i.e. the lessons through the destruction of the earlier generations. Then He said {كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا}, i.e. 'many We destroyed', so «كم» is an object of «أهلكنا», and the sentence is as though it explains the object omitted for «يَهْدِ»."
His saying: {مِّنَ القرون}: in the position of accusative as an adjective of «كم», because it is indefinite. Making it a ḥāl from an indefinite is weak. It is not permissible for it to be a tamyīz according to the rules of the Basrans, and «من» enters it as it enters other specifiers, because it is definite.
The majority read «يَهْدِ» with the third-person yāʾ. The discussion of its agent has preceded. Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān read it with the nūn that signals veneration, which supports the agent in the majority reading being the pronoun of Allah the Exalted.
