His saying: {يَمْشُونَ}: a ḥāl of «القرون» or of the object of «أهلكنا». On these two the pronoun refers to the destroyed generations. Its meaning: "We destroyed them while they were in a state of security, walking about and moving in their needs", like His saying {أَخَذْنَاهُمْ بَغْتَةً} [al-Anʿām: 44]. It may be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «لهم». The pronoun in «يَمْشُون» on this refers to whom the pronoun in «لهم» refers, namely the idolaters contemporary with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The governing word in it is «يَهْدِ». The meaning: that you walk in the dwellings of past nations and move about in their lands, so you should take heed lest there befall you what befell them. Ibn al-Sumayfiʿ read «يُمَشَّوْن» in the passive with doubling; since it became transitive by doubling, building it in the passive was permissible.

semin-durr:129-129.t:
His saying: {وَأَجَلٌ مُّسَمًّى}: there are two views on its nominative. The clearer: that it is conjoined to «كلمةٌ», i.e. "and had it not been for a fixed term, the punishment would have been binding on them".
The second, which al-Zamakhsharī allowed: that it is nominative, conjoined to the latent pronoun. The pronoun refers to the immediate seizure, indicated by the context. The separation by the genitive phrase stands in the place of emphasis. The implied form: "Had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, the immediate seizure and a fixed term would have been binding on them, as the two were binding on ʿĀd and Thamūd, and the fixed term would not have been alone without the immediate seizure."
I say: he made the ism of «كان» refer to what the context indicates, except that a problem arises for him: he allowed two views for «لزام». One: that it is the maṣdar of «لازَمَ», like «الخِصام», and there is no problem on this. The second: that it is an adjective of the pattern «فِعال» meaning «مُفْعِل», i.e. "making binding", as though it were an instrument of adherence because of the excess of its adherence, as they said «لِزازُ خَصْمٍ». On this it would be said that it should agree in the dual, saying «لِزَامَيْنِ», unlike its being a maṣdar, which is singular in every case.
Abū l-Baqāʾ allowed that «لزاماً» be the plural of «لازم», like «قِيام» plural of «قائم».

semin-durr:130-130.t:
His saying: {بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ}: a ḥāl, i.e. "while you are praising Him".
His saying {وَمِنْ آنَآءِ الليل}: attached to the second «سَبِّحْ». What concerns this fāʾ has been discussed.
His saying: {وَأَطْرَافَ}: the majority read it accusative. There are two views on it. One: that it is conjoined to the position of {وَمِنْ آنَآءِ الليل}. The second: that it is conjoined to «قبلَ». al-Ḥasan and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read «وأطرافِ» genitive, conjoined to «آناءِ الليل». His saying here «أطرافَ», and in Hūd {طَرَفَيِ النهار} [verse 114]: it is said that this is putting the plural in place of the dual, as in the saying: 3329 - «ظَرْاهما مثلُ ظُهورِ التُّرْسَيْنْ» (the two of them, their upper sides are like the backs of two shields). It is also said that it is in its true sense, and that what is meant by «الأطراف» is the hours.
His saying: {ترضى}: al-Kisāʾī and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read «تُرْضَى» in the passive. The rest read it in the active, and on this is {وَلَسَوْفَ يُعْطِيكَ رَبُّكَ فترضى} [al-Ḍuḥā: 5].

semin-durr:131-131.t:
His saying: {أَزْوَاجاً}: there are two views on its accusative. One: that it is accusative as a direct object, and that is clear. The second: that it is accusative as a ḥāl from the hāʾ in «به». He took into account the wording of «ما» once and its meaning another time, and therefore he made it plural. al-Zamakhsharī said: "...and the verb falls on «منهم»." al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is as though it were said: 'to that which We gave enjoyment of, namely kinds of some of them, and people from among them.'"
His saying: {زَهْرَةَ}: nine views on its accusative. One: that it is a second object, because «مَتَّعْنا» is made to include the sense of «أَعْطَيْنا»; so «أزواجاً» is the first object and «زهرةَ» the second. The second: that it is a badal of «أَزْواجاً», either with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "possessors of splendour", or by way of exaggeration, they being made the very splendour. The third: that it is accusative by an implied verb which «مَتَّعْنا» indicates, implied as "We made for them splendour". The third (again, as numbered in the source): accusative as blame (dhamm); al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is the accusative of specification (ikhtiṣāṣ)." The fourth: that it is a badal of the position of the relative. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "Some preferred it. Others said: it is not permissible, because His saying {لِنَفْتِنَهُمْ} belongs to the ṣila of «مَتَّعْنا», so there would be a separation between the ṣila and the relative by a foreigner." This is a fine objection.
The fifth: that it is accusative as a badal of the position of «به». The sixth: that it is accusative as a ḥāl of the relative «ما». The seventh: that it is a ḥāl of the hāʾ in «به», which is the pronoun of the relative, so it is like the preceding in meaning. If it is asked: how can a ḥāl be definite? The answer is that «زهرةَ» is made an indefinite with tanwīn, the tanwīn having been dropped only because of the meeting of two sukūns, as in: 3330 - «. . . . . . . . ولا ذاكرَ اللَّهَ إلاَّ قليلا» (. . . and not mentioning Allah except little). On this, why is «الحياة» genitive? It is said: as a badal of the relative «ما». The eighth: that it is a tamyīz for «ما» or for the hāʾ in «به»; so said al-Farrāʾ. They rejected it from him because it is definite, and a specifier is not definite. This is not binding on him, for making the specifier definite is permissible by the principles of the Kufans.
The ninth: that it is an adjective of «أَزْواجاً» through the two interpretations mentioned for its accusative as ḥāl. Abū l-Baqāʾ barred this view because the described is indefinite and the description definite, and this is answered as the answer given to justify its accusative as ḥāl, namely the dropping of the tanwīn because of the meeting of two sukūns.
The majority put sukūn on the hāʾ. al-Ḥasan, Abū l-Barhasam and Abū Ḥaywa read it with fatḥa; it is said: with the same meaning, like «جَهْرَة» and «جَهَرَة». al-Zamakhsharī allowed that it be the plural of «زاهر», like «فاجِر» and «فَجَرة», and «بارّ» and «بَرَرَة». al-Aṣmaʿī reported from Nāfiʿ «لنُفْتِنَهم» with ḍamma on the nūn, from «أَفْتَنَه», when he threw him into trial.
«الزَّهْرَة», with fatḥa on the hāʾ and with sukūn, like «نَهْر» and «نَهَر», is whatever delights of blossom. A lamp is «زاهر» for its gleam, a man «أزهر» and a woman «زهراء» from this. «الأنجمُ الزهرُ» are the shining stars.

semin-durr:132-132.t: His saying: {للتقوى}: i.e. "for the people of piety". This is supported by His saying in another place {والعاقبة لِلْمُتَّقِينَ} [al-Aʿrāf: 128]. Ibn Wathāb read «نَرْزقُك» assimilating the qāf into the kāf. The well-known view from him is that he assimilates only when the kāf is attached to the plural mīm, as in {خَلَقَكُمْ} [al-Baqara: 21], and that has been discussed.

semin-durr:133-133.t:
His saying: {أَوَلَمْ تَأْتِهِمْ بَيِّنَةُ}: Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr and Ḥafṣ read «تأتهم» with the feminine; the rest read it with the lower yāʾ, because the feminine is figurative. The majority read «بَيِّنَةُ ما» with «بَيِّنَة» annexed to «ما», nominative, and that is clear. Abū ʿAmr, in what Abū Zayd reported, read «بَيِّنَةٌ» with tanwīn, nominative. On this reading there are several views about «ما». One: that it is a badal of «بَيِّنَةٌ», a total substitute (badal kull min kull). The second: that it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is what is in the former scriptures". The third: that «ما» is negative. The author of «al-Lawāmiḥ» said: "What is meant is what is in the Qurʾān of abrogating verses and decisive statement, which was not in other books."
A group read «بَيِّنَةً» with tanwīn and accusative. Its explanation is that «ما» is the agent and «بَيِّنَةً» accusative as a ḥāl, made feminine according to the meaning of «ما». Whoever read with the feminine tāʾ did so by carrying it over to the meaning of «ما», and whoever read with the yāʾ did so according to its wording.
Ibn ʿAbbās read it with sukūn on the ḥāʾ. [Translator's note: the source gives no word for this reading; presumably «الصُّحْف»/«الصُّحُف» is meant.]

semin-durr:134-134.t:
The hāʾ in «قَبْلِهِ» may refer to the Messenger, by the evidence of His saying {لولا أَرْسَلْتَ إِلَيْنَا رَسُولاً}. al-Zamakhsharī and others allowed that it refer to «بَيِّنَةٍ», considering that it has the meaning of proof and evidence.
His saying: {فَنَتَّبِعَ}: accusative by an implied «أَنْ» in the response to urging (taḥḍīḍ). In the iʿrāb of Abū l-Baqāʾ it is "in the response to the question", which is an oversight.
Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn al-Ḥanafiyya, al-Ḥasan and a great many others read «نُذَلَّ ونخزى», both in the passive.

semin-durr:135-135.t:
And «مُتَرَبِّصٌ» is the khabar of «كل»; it is singular, carried over onto the wording of «كل».
His saying: {مَنْ أَصْحَابُ}: two views are allowed for this «مَنْ». The clearer: that it is interrogative, a mubtadaʾ, with «أصحابُ» its khabar, and the sentence is in the position of accusative, filling the place of the two objects. The second, attributed to al-Farrāʾ: that it is relative, meaning «الذين», and «أصحابُ» is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they are the companions"; this follows their school, since they omit such a returning pronoun even when the ṣila is not long. Then «عَلِمَ» may be of acquaintance (ʿirfāniyya), so it is content with this one object, or it may be in its usual sense, in which case the second must be implied.
The majority read «السَّوِيِّ» on the pattern «فَعيل», meaning "level". Abū Mijlaz and ʿImrān ibn Ḥudayr read «السَّواء» with fatḥa on the sīn and lengthening, meaning the good middle. Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar and al-Jaḥdarī read «السوءى» on the pattern «فعلى», considering that «الصراط» is treated as masculine and feminine. Ibn ʿAbbās read «السَّوْء» with fatḥa on the sīn, meaning evil.
It was reported from the two of them «السوى» with ḍamma on the sīn and shadda on the wāw. This allows two views. One: that he turned the hamza into wāw and assimilated the wāw into the wāw. The other: that it is «فُعْلى» from «السَّواء», its origin being «السُّوْيا», the yāʾ turned into wāw and also assimilated. The analogical form would be «السُّيَّا», because whenever a yāʾ and a wāw meet and the first is preceded by sukūn, the wāw is turned into yāʾ; here the opposite was done.
«السُّوَيِّ» has also been read with ḍamma on the sīn, fatḥa on the wāw and shadda on the yāʾ, a diminutive of «سُوْء»; so said al-Zamakhsharī. The Shaykh said: "It is not good, for if it were so the hamza of «سوء» would remain. The better view is that it is the diminutive of «سواء», like their saying «عُطَيّ» for «عَطاء»." I say: Abū l-Baqāʾ also made it the diminutive of «السَّوْء», meaning with fatḥa on the sīn. The objection raised against al-Zamakhsharī applies to him, but replacing a hamza of this kind is permissible, so there is no objection.
His saying: {وَمَنِ اهتدى}: three views. One: that it is interrogative, and its rule is like that of the one before it, except for the omission of the returning pronoun. The second: that it is in the position of nominative, as explained for the interrogative. The third: that it is in the position of genitive, a conjunction on «الصراطِ», i.e. "and the companions of him who was guided". On these last two views it is relative. Abū l-Baqāʾ said of the second view: "In it is the conjoining of a declarative to an interrogative, and in it is a strengthening of the saying of al-Farrāʾ", meaning that if he makes it relative it is declarative.

semin-durr:1-1.t:
The discussion of the disjoined letters came at the beginning of this topic, and "طه" is of that kind; this is the correct view. It has also been said that the meaning of "طه" is "O man" in the language of ʿAkk, or it is said ʿUkl, or it is said that it is a Yemeni language. Al-Kalbī related that if you said in ʿAkk "O man", he would not answer until you said "ṭā-hā".
Al-Ṭabarī said: "'طه' in ʿAkk means 'O man'", and cited the saying of their poet:
3269 - دَعَوْتُ بِطهَ في القتالِ فلم يُجِبْ ... فَخِفْتُ عليهِ أَنْ يكونَ مُوائِلا
(I called "Ṭā-hā" in the fighting and he did not answer, so I feared for him that he had sought refuge.) And the saying of another:
3270 - إنَّ السَّفاهةَ طه في خلائِقِكمْ ... لا قَدَّسَ اللهُ أرواحَ المَلاعينِ
(Indeed foolishness, O man, is in your natures; may Allah not sanctify the spirits of the accursed.)
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The trace of artifice is apparent in the verse cited as evidence", and he mentioned it. Al-Suddī said: "its meaning is 'O so-and-so'." Al-Zamakhsharī also said: "Perhaps ʿAkk altered 'yā hādhā', as though in their language they turn the yā' into ṭā', saying ṭā for yā, and abbreviated 'hādhā' to 'hā'." He means that it is as though the noble verse said "O this one". There is great remoteness in this.
The Shaykh said: "Then he conjectured and guessed about ʿAkk what no grammarian had said: that they turn the vocative yā into ṭā' and drop the demonstrative noun, keeping only the 'hā' of attention." I say: though this is close to what he said about him, he was harsh on him in his wording with "he conjectured".
It has also been said: "طه" is originally "طَأْها" with a hamza, "طَأْ" being an imperative from وَطِىء يَطَأُ ("to tread"), and "ها" an object pronoun returning to the earth; then the hamza was turned into an alif because of its sukūn, and it was not dropped in the imperative, having regard to its origin; that is: "tread the earth with your feet". It has come in exegesis: "He stood until his feet swelled."
Al-Ḥasan, ʿIkrima, Abū Ḥanīfa and Warsh in his own choice read it dropping the alif after the ṭā', with a hā' with sukūn. It has two views. One: the original is "طَأْ" with a hamza, also an imperative from وَطِىء يَطَأُ, then the hamza was turned into a hā', as they turned it in "هَرَقْتُ", "هَرَحْتُ" and "هَبَرْتُ", the originals being أَرَقْتُ, أَرَحْتُ and أَبَرْت. The other: the hamza was turned into an alif, as though he took it from وَطِي يَطا with the substitution, as in:
3271 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . لا هَنَاكِ المَرْتَعُ
(...may the pasture not be pleasant for you.) [Translator's note: the first hemistich is elided in the source.] then the alif was dropped, carrying the imperative over to the jussive and ignoring the origin of the hamza, then the hā' of pause was attached, and continuous reading was treated like pausing. The discussion of the imāla of "ṭā" and "hā" came at the beginning of Yūnus, which makes repeating it here unnecessary.

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying: {أَنَزَلْنَا}: this is the reading of the majority. Ṭalḥa read "ما نُزِّلَ" as a passive, with "القرآنُ" nominative because it stands in for the agent.
This sentence may be resumptive if "طه" is made an enumeration of the names of letters; it may be the khabar of "طه" if you make it the name of the sūra, in which case "القرآن" is an overt noun standing in the place of the pronoun, because "طه" is also a Qur'an; and it may be the answer to an oath, if you make "طه" the thing sworn by. The detailed discussion of this has already come.

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {إِلاَّ تَذْكِرَةً}: There are several views on its accusative. One: it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and the governing word in it is the verb of sending down; likewise "تَشقى" is also a reason for it. The first must come with a lām because it is not the agent of the verb being explained, so it lacks the condition for being accusative as an object; the second may have the lām cut off and be accusative, since it fulfils the conditions. This is al-Zamakhsharī's statement, and then he said: "If you ask: 'May you say: "We did not send down ... that you be wretched" as in {أَن تَحْبَطَ أَعْمَالُكُمْ} [al-Ḥujurāt: 2]?' I say: yes, but this is an incidental accusative, like the accusative in {واختار موسى قَوْمَهُ} [al-Aʿrāf: 155]; as for the accusative in 'تَذْكِرةً', it is like that in 'I struck Zayd', because it is one of the five objects that are the principles and canons for the rest."
I say: Abū l-Baqāʾ forbade "تَذْكرةً" being a mafʿūl li-ajlihi of the "أَنْزَلْنا" mentioned, because it has already reached one object of purpose, namely "لتشقى", so it does not reach another of the same kind. This prohibition is nothing, because it is permissible to give a verb two or more reasons; this is built from him on the view that the governing word of these optional complements reaches only one, except through badal or conjunction.
Two: "تذكرة" is a badal for the position of "لِتَشْقَى", which is the view of al-Zajjāj, followed by Ibn ʿAṭiyya; Abū Jaʿfar found it unlikely, and al-Fārisī rejected it because the reminder is not wretchedness. This is a clear rejection. Al-Zamakhsharī clarified this, saying: "If you ask: 'May "تذكرةً" be a badal for the position of "لِتشقى"?' I say: no, because of the difference of the two kinds; rather it is accusative as a disconnected exception in which 'إلاَّ' has the sense of 'لكن'."
The Shaykh said: "He means by the difference of the two kinds that the accusative of 'تذكرةً' is a sound accusative, not incidental, while the accusative that is in 'لِتشقى' after removal of the preposition is an incidental accusative. And we say that it has no position at all, so a badal for it cannot be imagined." I say: al-Zamakhsharī means by the difference of the two kinds only what I mentioned from al-Fārisī in refutation of al-Zajjāj; and what effect does the difference of the two accusatives have in that?
Three: it is accusative as a disconnected exception, that is: "but We sent it down as a reminder". Four: it is a corroborating maṣdar of an implied verb, that is: "but We reminded", or "be reminded by it, you, as a reminder". Five: it is a maṣdar in the position of ḥāl, that is: "except as a reminder (mudhakkiran)". Six: it is a badal for "القرآن", the Qur'an being the reminder; so said al-Ḥawfī. Seven: it is also a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, but the governing word in it is "لِتَشْقَى", and the meaning is as al-Zamakhsharī said: "We sent down the Qur'an to you that you bear the hardships of conveying the message, of disputing with the tyrants among the enemies of Islam and fighting them, and other kinds of toil and the burdens of prophethood; and We did not send down this wearisome toil upon you except that it be a reminder.
On this view 'تذكرة' may be a ḥāl and a mafʿūl li-ajlihi." End.
If you ask: whence did you take it that, when he made it a ḥāl and a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, the governing word in it is "لِتَشْقَى"? What prevents him from meaning by the governing word the verb of sending down? The answer is that this view came earlier from him in his saying "each one of 'لتشقى' and 'تذكرة' is a reason for the verb". Moreover his interpretation of the meaning mentioned rests on "لِتَشْقَى" governing "تذكرة". But since this meaning that appeared to al-Zamakhsharī did not appear to Abū l-Baqāʾ, he forbade "لِتَشْقَى" governing "تذكرة", saying: "It is not sound that 'لِتَشْقى' govern it, because of the corruption of the meaning." The answer to him is what came earlier. And there is nothing strange in calling toil "shaqāʾ"; al-Zamakhsharī said: "'الشقاءُ' comes in the sense of toil. From it is the proverb: 'More wearying than the breaker of a colt' and 'more wretched than the breaker of a colt'."
{لِّمَن يخشى} is attached to "تذكرةً". The lām was added to the object to strengthen the governing word since it is derivative; it may also be attached to an omitted element as an adjective of "تذكرةً".

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {تَنزِيلاً}: There are several views on its accusative. One: it is a badal for "تذكرةً" if that is made a ḥāl, not if it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, because a thing is not given itself as its reason. I say: because the implied form would become: "We did not send down the Qur'an except for the sending down." Two: it is accusative through an implied "نزَّل". Three: it is accusative through "أَنْزَلْنا", because the meaning of "We did not send it down except as a reminder" is "We sent it down as a reminder". Four: it is accusative as praise and specification (madḥ wa-ikhtiṣāṣ).
Five: it is accusative through "يخشى" as a direct object, that is: "He sent it down as a reminder for whoever fears the sending down of Allah", which is a fine meaning and a clear i'rab.
The Shaykh said, and he was not fair to him: "The best is what we mentioned first, that it is accusative through an implied 'نزَّل'. What al-Zamakhsharī mentioned of its being accusative otherwise is strained. As for the first, it makes 'تذكرةً' and 'تنزيلاً' two ḥāls, though they are two maṣdars, and making a maṣdar a ḥāl is not analogical.
Moreover the referent of 'تذكرةً' is not the referent of 'تنزيل', and 'تنزيلاً' is not part of a 'تذكرة'. If it is a badal, it would be a badal ishtimāl on the view of those who hold that the second includes the first, because the sending down includes the reminder and other things. As for his saying 'because the meaning of "We did not send it down except as a reminder" is "We sent it down as a reminder"', it is not so, because the meaning of restriction is lost in his saying 'We sent it down as a reminder'. As for its being accusative as praise, that is remote. As for its being accusative through 'يخشى', that is extremely remote, because 'يخشى' is the head of a verse and a pause, so it does not suit 'تنزيلاً' to be accusative through 'يخشى'; and his saying about it 'it is fine and a clear i'rab' is a foreignness (ʿujma) and a distance from grasping eloquence."
I say: it is enough for him that he rejects the obvious without proof, and attributes to this man lack of eloquence and the presence of foreignness.
His saying: {مِّمَّنْ خَلَق}: "مِنْ" may be attached to "تنزيلاً", or to an omitted element as an adjective of "تنزيلاً". In "خَلَق" there is an iltifāt from the first person in His saying "أَنْزَلْنا" to the third. Al-Zamakhsharī allowed that "ما أنزَلْنا" be a report of the speech of Gabriel and some of the angels, in which case there is no iltifāt.
His saying: {العلى} is the plural of عُلْيا, like دنيا and دُنا. Its parallel among sound forms is كُبْرى and كُبَر, فُضْلى and فُضَل.

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {الرحمن}: The majority read it in the nominative, with several views. One: it is a badal for the latent pronoun in "خَلَق"; Ibn ʿAṭiyya mentioned it. The Shaykh rejected it because a badal takes the place of what it replaces, and if it took its place here it would not be permissible, because the sentence attached to the relative would lack a link tying it to it. Two: it is nominative as khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, whose implied form is "He is the Merciful". Three: it is nominative as mubtadaʾ, its lām pointing to "مَنْ خَلَقَ", and the sentence after it is its khabar.
Janāḥ ibn Ḥubaysh read "الرحمنِ" in the genitive. There are two views. One: it is a badal for the relative. It is not to be said that this leads to a badal with a derived noun, which is rare, because "الرحمن" has come to be treated as a non-derived noun through its frequent following of governing words. Two: it is also an adjective of the relative.
The Shaykh said: "The school of the Kufans is that the incomplete nouns like 'مَنْ' and 'ما' are not qualified by adjectives, with 'الذي' alone excepted; so on their school it is not permissible that it be an adjective." He said that as a rejection of al-Zamakhsharī.
The sentence {عَلَى العرش استوى} is the khabar of His saying "الرحمنُ" on the view that it is a mubtadaʾ, or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ if it is said to be nominative as khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, and likewise in the reading of the one who makes it genitive.
The agent of "استوى" is a pronoun returning to "الرحمن". It has also been said that its agent is the relative "ما" after it, that is: "he who has what is in the heavens settled". Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "Some extremists say that 'ما' is the agent of 'استوى'. This is remote, and moreover it does not help him in the interpretation, since His saying {الرحمن عَلَى العرش} remains a complete statement, and from that he fled." I say: this is transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he used to pause at the word "العرش" and then begin "استوى له ما في السماوات", and this is not sound from him.

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {الثرى}: it is damp earth, and its lām is yā', as shown by its dual ثَرَيَيْن and their saying ثَرِيَتْ الأرَضُ تَثْرَى ثَرَىً. "الثرى" is used for the severing of affection. Jarīr said:
3272 - فلا تَنْبُشُوا بيني وبينَكُمُ الثرى ... فإنَّ الذي بيني وبينَكُمُ مُثْرِي
(Do not dig up the earth between me and you, for what is between me and you is moist/abundant.) And "الثَّراءُ" with madd is abundance of wealth. He said:
3273 - أَماوِيَّ ما يُغْني الثراءُ عن الفتى ... إذا حَشَرَجَتْ يوماً وضاقَ بها الصدرُ
(O Māwiyya, what does wealth avail a young man when one day the death-rattle sounds and his chest is constricted by it?)
How fine is the saying of Ibn Durayd:
3274 - يوماً تصيرُ إلى الثَّرى ... ويفوزُ غيرُك بالثَّراءِ
(One day you will go to the earth, and another than you will win the wealth.)
In this poem he combined the lengthened and the shortened with a difference of meaning.

semin-durr:7-7.t: His saying: {وأخفى}: they allowed two views in it. One: it is an elative, that is "and more hidden than the secret". Two: it is a past verb, that is: "and Allah hid His unseen from His servants", as in His saying: {وَلاَ يُحِيطُونَ بِهِ عِلْماً} [Ṭāhā: 110].

semin-durr:8-8.t: The Majestic Name is either a mubtadaʾ, with the negated sentence as its khabar, or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is "He is Allah". "الحُسْنى" is the feminine of الأحسن. It has been said more than once that the broken plural of non-rational beings is treated as a single feminine.

semin-durr:10-10.t:
His saying: {إِذْ رأى}: it may be accusative through "الحديث", which is the apparent view. It may also be accusative through an implied "اذكر" ("remember"), as Abū l-Baqāʾ said, or through an omitted element after it, that is: "when he saw a fire, such-and-such happened", as al-Zamakhsharī said.
"هل" is in its normal sense of an interrogative of affirmation (istifhām taqrīr); it has also been said to have the sense of "qad", and to have the sense of negation. Ḥamza read "لأهلِهُ امكثُوا" with ḍamma on the hā'; it has been mentioned that this is the original and the dialect of the Hijaz, while Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "the ḍamma is by assimilation (ittibāʿ)".
His saying: {آنَسْتُ} means "I saw". "الإِيناسُ" is clear seeing, and from it the "insān" of the eye (the pupil), because things are seen with it; it has also been said to be finding, and to be perceiving, which is more general than seeing. They recited the verse of al-Ḥārith ibn Ḥilliza:
3275 - آنسَتْ نَبْأَةً وأَفْزَعَها القُنْ ... ناصُ عَصْراً وقد دنا الإِمْساءُ
(She perceived a faint sound, and the hunter startled her in the afternoon, when evening had drawn near.)
"القَبَسُ" is a brand of fire, the flame at the head of a stick or reed and the like. It is a فَعَل with the sense of مَفْعول, like القَبَض and النَّقَض, meaning المَقْبوض and المَنْقوض. One says أَقْبَسْتُ الرجلَ علماً and قَبَسْتُه ناراً, distinguishing between the two; this is the view of al-Mubarrad. Al-Kisāʾī said: فَعَلَ and أَفْعَلَ are both said in the two meanings, so one says قَبَسْتُه ناراً وعلماً, and أَقْبَسْته also علماً وناراً.
His saying {مِّنْهَا} may be attached to "آتِيكم" or to an omitted element as ḥāl from "قَبَس". Some pronounced the alif of "هدى" with imāla in pause. The good practice is not to apply imāla, because the best-known view is that it is a substitute for tanwīn.

semin-durr:11-11.t: His saying: {نُودِيَ}: the one standing in for the agent is the pronoun of Mūsā; it has also been said to be the pronoun of the maṣdar, that is "the call was called", which is weak. They forbade the sentence "يا موسى" from being the one standing in for the agent, because a sentence cannot be an agent.

semin-durr:12-12.t:
His saying: {إني}: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read it with fatḥa, on the implied bā' ("بأني"), because the call is linked with it; you say "I called him with such-and-such". The poet said, as al-Fārisī recited:
3276 - نادَيْتُ باسمِ ربيعةَ بنِ مُكَدَّمٍ ... إنَّ المُنَوَّهَ باسمِه المَوْثُوْقُ
(I called by the name of Rabīʿa ibn Mukaddam: indeed the one whose name is proclaimed is the trusted.)
Ibn ʿAṭiyya allowed it to have the sense of "for the sake of", which is not apparent. The others read with kasra: either on an implied saying, as is the view of the Basrans, or because the call has the sense of saying according to the Kufans.
His saying: {أَنَاْ} may be a mubtadaʾ with what follows as its khabar, the sentence being the khabar of "إنَّ". It may also be an emphasis for the accusative pronoun, and may be a separating pronoun (faṣl).
His saying "طوى": the Kufans and Ibn ʿĀmir read "طُوىً" with ḍamma on the ṭā' and tanwīn. The others read it with ḍamma without tanwīn. Al-Ḥasan, al-Aʿmash, Abū Ḥaywa and Ibn Muḥayṣin read it with kasra on the ṭā' and tanwīn, and Abū Zayd from Abū ʿAmr with kasra without tanwīn.
Whoever read it with ḍamma and tanwīn made it inflected because he interpreted it as the place. Whoever withheld the tanwīn has several possibilities. One: he withheld it for feminine gender in the sense of the tract of land, together with being a proper name. Two: he withheld it for ʿadl (deviation) to the pattern فُعَل, even though the word it deviated from is not known, treating it like عُمَر and زُفَر. Three: it is a foreign noun, so its withholding is for being a proper name and foreign.
Whoever read it with kasra without tanwīn did so also in regard to the tract of land. If it is a noun, it is like عِنَب; if an adjective, like عِدَى and سِوَى. Whoever gave it tanwīn did so in regard to the place. From al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī: it has the sense of الثنى with kasra and shortening, and الثنى is what is repeated twice, so the meaning of this reading is that it appeared twice, and it would be a maṣdar accusative through the word "المقدَّس" because it has its meaning, as if it were said: "sanctified twice", from التقديس.
ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and al-Ḍaḥḥāk read "طاوِيْ اذهَبْ".
"طوى" is either a badal for "الوادي", or an ʿaṭf bayān for it, or nominative with an implied mubtadaʾ, or accusative with an implied "أعني" ("I mean").

semin-durr:13-13.t:
His saying: {وَأَنَا اخترتك}: Ḥamza, among others, read "وأنَّا اخترناك" with fatḥa on the hamza, with the pronoun of the speaker magnifying himself. Al-Sulamī, al-Aʿmash and Ibn Hurmuz read likewise, except that they put kasra on the hamza. The others read "وأنا اخْتَرْتُك" with the pronoun of the speaker alone. Ubayy read "وأني اخترتك" with fatḥa on the hamza.
As for Ḥamza's reading, it is conjoined to His saying {إني أَنَاْ رَبُّكَ}, which is with fatḥa on the hamza there, so he did that when he conjoined another to it. Whoever put kasra did so because he reads "إنِّي أنا ربك" with kasra. Ubayy's reading is like Ḥamza's with respect to the conjunction. Abū l-Baqāʾ allowed the fatḥa to be on the implied form "ولأنَّا اخترناك فاستمع" ("and because We chose you, so listen"), attaching it to "استمع". The first is preferable. The second object of "اخترتك" is omitted, that is: "I chose you from among your people".
His saying {لِمَا يوحى}: the apparent view is that it is attached to "استمِعْ". It is possible that the lām is added to the object, as in His saying {رَدِفَ لَكُم} [al-Naml: 72]. Al-Zamakhsharī and others allowed the case to be one of tanāzuʿ (competition) between "اخْتَرْتُك" and "استمع", as if it were said: "I chose you for what is revealed, so listen to what is revealed." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "So he attaches the lām to 'استمعْ' or to 'اخترتُك'."
The Shaykh rejected this, saying: "Attaching it to 'اخترتك' is not permissible because it belongs to the chapter of ʿamal (governing), where it is obligatory or preferred to repeat the pronoun with the second, which would give 'فاستمعْ له لِما يوحى'; which shows that it is a case of giving effect to the second." I say: al-Zamakhsharī meant the attachment in meaning, as to suitability; as for the technical posited form, he did not mean it.
"ما" may be a maṣdar, or have the sense of "الذي", that is: "so listen to the revelation, or to that which is revealed".

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying: {لذكري}: the maṣdar may be annexed to its agent, that is: "because I mentioned it in the Books", or "because I remember you". It may also be annexed to its object, that is: "that you remember Me". It has also been said that its meaning is remembering the prayer after forgetting it, as in his saying, peace be upon him: "Whoever sleeps through a prayer or forgets it, let him pray it when he remembers it." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The proper wording would have been 'لذكرها'". Then he said: "Whoever strains for it may say: when he remembers the prayer he has remembered [Allah]; or on an omitted muḍāf, that is 'for the remembrance of My prayer'; or because remembrance and forgetting are from Allah the Exalted in reality."
Abū Rajāʾ and al-Sulamī read "للذكرى" with the lām of definiteness and the alif of feminine ending. Some read "لذكرى" indefinite, and some "للذكر" definite and masculine.
His saying: {أَكَادُ أُخْفِيهَا}: The majority read "أُخْفيها" with ḍamma on the hamza. There are several interpretations. One: the hamza in "أُخْفيها" is for privation and removal, that is "I remove its concealment", like أعجمتُ الكتابَ, "I removed its non-Arabic quality". There are then two senses to that. One: that "الخفاء" has the sense of covering, and when He removes its covering He has manifested it. The meaning: because it is certain to happen and near, I almost reveal it, were it not for what wisdom requires of delay. The other: that "الخفاء" is appearance, as will come. The meaning: I remove its appearance, and when He removes its appearance it is hidden. The meaning: because of the intensity of its obscurity I almost hide it so that I do not reveal it at all, though it must be revealed; and for that reason it is found in some codices, such as Ubayy's codex: "I almost hide it from Myself, so how would I show you it?" That is in keeping with the Arabs' habit of exaggeration in concealment. He said:
3277 - أيامَ تَصْحَبُني هندٌ وأُخْبِرُها ... ما كِدْت أكتُمُه عني من الخبرِ
(In the days when Hind accompanied me and I told her what I almost concealed even from myself of news.)
And how can concealing from oneself be imagined?
The second interpretation: "كاد" is redundant; so said Ibn Jubayr. Another cited as evidence the saying of Zayd al-Khayl:
3278 - سريعٌ إلى الهَيْجاء شاكٍ سلاحُه ... فما إنْ يكادُ قِرْنُه يتنفَّسُ
(Quick to battle, his weapons bristling, so that his opponent scarcely breathes.)
And another said:
3279 - وألاَّ ألومَ النفسَ فيما أصابني ... وألا أكادَ بالذي نِلْتُ أَبْجَحُ
(That I not blame myself for what befell me, and that I not exult at what I obtained.)
There is no proof in any of this.
The third interpretation: that "الكَيْدُوْدَة" has the sense of intending; it is ascribed to al-Akhfash and a group, and it does not serve what they intended.
The fourth interpretation: that its khabar is omitted, its implied form being: "I almost bring it, because of its nearness." They cited the saying of Ḍābiʾ al-Burjumī:
3280 - هَمَمْتُ ولم أفْعَلْ وكِدْتُ وليتني ... تَرَكْتُ على عثمانَ تَبْكي حلائِلُهْ
(I intended and did not do it, and I almost did; would that I had left ʿUthmān with his wives weeping over him.)
that is: "and I almost did", so the pause is on "أكادُ" and the beginning is with "أُخْفيها"; Abū Jaʿfar approved of it.
Abū l-Dardāʾ, Ibn Jubayr, al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid and Ḥumayd read "أَخْفيها" with fatḥa on the hamza. The meaning: "I reveal it", by the interpretation given before. One says خَفَيْتُ الشيءَ, "I revealed it", and أَخْفَيْتُه, "I concealed it"; this is the well-known view. It was transmitted from Abū l-Khaṭṭāb that خَفَيْتُ and أَخْفَيْتُ have one meaning. It was related from Abū ʿUbayd that "أَخْفى" is one of the words of opposite meanings, meaning both "revealed" and "concealed", and on this the two readings are the same. An example of خَفَيْتُ in the sense of "I revealed" is the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
3281 - خَفَاهُنَّ مِنْ أَنْفاقِهِنَّ كأنما ... خفاهُنَّ وَدْقٌ مِنْ عَشِيٍّ مُجَلِّبِ
(He brought them out of their burrows, as though a downpour from a thundering evening had brought them out.)
and the saying of another:
3282 - فإنْ تَدْفِنوا الداءَ لا نَخْفِهِ ... وإنْ تُوْقِدُوْا الحربَ لا نَقْعُدِ
(If you bury the disease we shall not unearth it, and if you kindle the war we shall not sit still.)
His saying: {لتجزى}: this is the lām of purpose (lām kay), and does not have the sense of an oath, that is "لَتُجْزَيَنَّ", as Abū l-Baqāʾ transmitted from some. This lām is attached to "اُخْفيها". Some made it attached to "آتيةٌ", but this is not complete unless you posit that "أكاد أُخْفيها" is a parenthetical clause between what is attached and what it is attached to; but if you make it an adjective of "آتِيَةٌ" it does not work on the school of the Basrans, because an active participle, when it is qualified, does not govern, though if it governed and was then qualified it would be permissible.
Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is also said to be attached to 'آتِيَةٌ', and for that reason some paused on it with a slight pause, to signal its separation from 'أخفيها'."
His saying: {بِمَا تسعى} is attached to "تجزى". "ما" may be a maṣdar or a nominal relative, and a muḍāf is necessary, that is: "she is requited with the punishment for her striving", or "with the punishment for what she strove".
